<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1. </span>The panel against its own naive vote</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Which panel is on offer must be established first, and the answer is not the obvious one: combining the ten votes naively gives a panel that has to be rescued from itself.
Wherever competence is concentrated in one leader or spread unevenly across a field with actively harmful members, the unweighted majority panel sits <em id="S3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">significantly below</em> the best single judge –by <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.094" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.094</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.094</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.228" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.228</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.228</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>, <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>, <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, and <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>– because the weaker, mutually redundant members outvote the few capable ones.
Stacking reverses this: reading the <em id="S3.SS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">unw.</em> and <em id="S3.SS1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">stacked</em> columns of Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> against <em id="S3.SS1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">best (CV)</em>, the panel is no longer clearly below the best single judge on any of the four, and the paired delta <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text">(stacked <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> unweighted)</span> is significantly positive on each (up to <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.279" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.279</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.279</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>) and borderline on <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> (intervals in Appendix <a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>, Table <a href="#A9.T17" title="Table 17 ‣ Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>).
The effect is, by contrast, small or absent where the naive vote is not clearly below the best single judge, i.e. where competence is spread (<span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>, <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span>) or redundant (<span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>); the size of the rescue thus depends on how heterogeneous the members are.
Weighting each vote by that member’s own agreement with gold (each in isolation) gives the graded form of the same point: both accuracy- and log-odds-weighted voting sit below the stacker on every dataset (Appendix <a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Comparison with an unsupervised aggregator.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A sharper test than the naive vote is another <em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">aggregator</em> over the same ten votes, and the natural choice is the model of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dawid and Skene [13]</a></cite> (<em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">D–S</em>), which estimates each member’s reliability without gold and so isolates what the labels buy (Appendix <a href="#A12" title="Appendix L Extended related work ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">L</span></a>).
The stacked panel is never significantly beaten by it (Appendix <a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>), and the delta <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text">(stacked <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> DS)</span> offers a clear improvement on <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>, <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>, and <span id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, and straddles zero elsewhere;
D–S itself falls significantly below the CV-best single wherever the best member must be picked out of a weak or correlated field.
This is the competence/correlation account (§<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> below) seen from the aggregator side: where errors decorrelate and competence is spread, an unsupervised aggregator suffices; if one judge must be recovered, only supervised re-weighting does.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2. </span>The panel against the best single judge</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Against the fair (CV-best) baseline, the paired difference is an improvement on all four core grounded datasets, and on one of them it is clear:
<span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> offers a delta <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text">(stacked <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> best single) <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=+0.032" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.032</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=+0.032</annotation></semantics></math></span> clear against both the CV-best and the oracle (<span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Granite</span>) –the suite’s one <em id="S3.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">clean win</em> in the sense of §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Metrics and the decision rule. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>– and still clear on the items the baseline commits on (<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.031" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.031</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.031</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[+0.003,+0.058]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.003</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.058</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[+0.003,+0.058]</annotation></semantics></math>); on the other three, the improvement stands but the sample does not resolve it.
A Holm correction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite> over the four core deltas (cf. §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" title="Benchmarks and judges. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) leaves that win significant (adjusted one-sided <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.048</annotation></semantics></math>), whereas over all eight it would not (<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.096</annotation></semantics></math>, see also Appendix <a href="#A11" title="Appendix K Judge roster, prompt, and coverage ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">K</span></a>).
With nine competent members under the claim-support frame (<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa\geq 0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa\geq 0.30</annotation></semantics></math>;
cf. Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a)) and the best single being already strong, <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> offers an unresolved improvement (<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.056" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.056</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.056</annotation></semantics></math>) at <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=222" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>222</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=222</annotation></semantics></math>.
On <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>, conversely, one member (<span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Gemma</span>) dominates a weak field and is reliably found by cross-validation, leaving almost no headroom (<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.010" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.010</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.010</annotation></semantics></math>).
Finally, on <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span> the members carry moderate, redundant competence (four at <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa\geq 0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa\geq 0.30</annotation></semantics></math>) and the edge (<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.037" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.037</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.037</annotation></semantics></math>, one-sided <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.045" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.045</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.045</annotation></semantics></math>) is the suite’s closest unresolved improvement.
The two grounded sets held back are unresolved as well (<span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span> as an improvement and <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span> as a worsening), and are reported in Appendix <a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>.
This fixes the scope of the internal contest: the difference favours the panel on seven out of eight datasets, yet is clear on one core set of four.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Comparing baselines needing no per-dataset labels.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Identifying the best single, however, requires labels a deployer might not have; against the baselines needing no such per-dataset selection (Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, leftmost block) the panel is strong wherever there is signal: it improves on the label-free average member by <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.082" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.082</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.082</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.261" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.261</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.261</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, clearly on every dataset in the suite, and is nowhere clearly below the single best-on-average judge (<span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Gemma</span>).
The one-of-four verdict above is thus the same panel read against a baseline that has already spent those labels, and its position on that ladder is what §<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> prices.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3. </span>The competence/correlation account</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The pattern of paired differences above is not arbitrary:
it is ordered by two member-level quantities recovered from the calibration set the aggregator already requires, namely the <em id="S3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">distribution of competence</em> –how many members are individually capable, rather than how good the best one is– and the <em id="S3.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">correlation of errors</em> — whether the members, when wrong, are wrong on the same items, which we summarise by their mean pairwise error-correlation <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The ordering, however, does not rest on eight dataset points alone: restricting to the items on which the best single judge errs isolates the recovery the <em id="S3.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">other</em> members carry.
Under this framing, the panel recovers the item more often precisely when a larger fraction of members is individually correct on it (logistic regression with dataset fixed effects, coefficient <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+4.67" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>4.67</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+4.67</annotation></semantics></math>; point-biserial <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=+0.41" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.41</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=+0.41</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&lt;10^{-20}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&lt;10^{-20}</annotation></semantics></math>, positive within all eight datasets; Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>).
Distributed, decorrelated competence is thus what the panel harnesses, and what the stacker’s own weights reward in place of average accuracy (Appendix <a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>, Figure <a href="#A9.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.39229v1/fig_regime.svg" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:236/214;" width="236" height="214"></object></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.39229v1/fig_forest.svg" id="S3.F3.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:268/212;" width="268" height="212"></object></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F3.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>. </span><span id="S3.F3.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The regime ordering.
<span id="S3.F3.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> The eight datasets (markers) scattered by the members’ mean pairwise error-correlation <math id="S3.F3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S3.F3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis) against the number of members at <math id="S3.F3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa\geq\kappa_{0}=0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa\geq\kappa_{0}=0.30</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S3.F3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-axis).
The gold lines are the thresholds <math id="S3.F3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}=0.40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.40</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}=0.40</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.F3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=\nicefrac{{1}}{{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded voffset="0.3em"><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mpadded><mpadded style="width:-0.15em;" lspace="-0.1em" width="-0.15em"><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true">/</mo></mpadded><mn mathsize="0.700em">2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=\nicefrac{{1}}{{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> (five members), and bound the admissible region (shaded quadrant);
the hatched area is the invariance region, the positions of the gold point at which no dataset changes side, unbounded to the right.
Varying <math id="S3.F3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> moves the points rather than an edge (Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>).
<span id="S3.F3.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> The panel’s paired delta against the CV-best single (<math id="S3.F3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bullet" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bullet</annotation></semantics></math>), the average member (<math id="S3.F3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\blacksquare</annotation></semantics></math>), and the frontier judge (<math id="S3.F3.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blackdiamond" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>�</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\blackdiamond</annotation></semantics></math>), reported per dataset with <math id="S3.F3.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo mathsize="1.110em">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> paired cluster-bootstrap intervals.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The two coordinates order the suite, and Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a) places the eight datasets in the plane they span (qualitatively, eight points being too few to resolve either coordinate statistically, cf. Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>, Table <a href="#A2.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Cross-dataset predictor (illustrative only). ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).
The panel’s improvement over the best single is largest where competence is distributed over several capable members whose errors decorrelate, shrinks where that competence is moderate and mutually redundant, and vanishes where one model dominates a weak field.
The same ordering governs the frontier comparison.
Read against all three comparators at once (Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(b)), the difference over the <em id="S3.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">best</em> single narrows to zero as one model comes to dominate, and the difference against the <em id="S3.SS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">frontier</em> judge worsens along with it (§<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> below), while the difference over the <em id="S3.SS3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">average</em> member does neither, staying uniformly large wherever there is signal.
The regime in which a panel improves on its own leader is thus also one in which the frontier is not materially ahead.
The frontier has to be kept only in the dominant-leader regime the test rejects, which is why we answer the two questions together.
Interestingly, it is not the regime the literature would predict:
grounded-versus-ungrounded is numerically present but mechanistically empty, the two ungrounded sets falling in <em id="S3.SS3.p2.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">opposite</em> regimes, and what moves with the task is instead the identity of the best single judge — which is what a panel is meant to supply, and what fails to transfer (Appendices <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> and <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Transfer to an unseen dataset ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The admissibility test.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The account enters the method only if a deployer can tell, on a new task, which side of it they are on:
this is the second component of RAIM (§<a href="#S1" title="1. Introduction ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>), which, along with the stacker’s down-weighting of redundant members, makes the scheme <span id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">robust</span>.
The test reads the two coordinates off the calibration set, and admits a task when enough members are competent and their errors are weakly correlated.
Formally, given a competence bar <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, a share <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>, and a correlation bar <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, a task is <em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">admissible</em> when at least a share <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> of the members reach <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa\geq\kappa_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa\geq\kappa_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}\leq\phi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}\leq\phi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>;
in the plane of Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a), at fixed <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, this is a quadrant, and, in what follows, we adopt <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\kappa_{0},c,\phi_{0})=(0.30,\tfrac{1}{2},0.40)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.30</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mn>0.40</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\kappa_{0},c,\phi_{0})=(0.30,\tfrac{1}{2},0.40)</annotation></semantics></math> as an operating point, resulting in <span id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, <span id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>, and <span id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> being admitted.
Tightening any of the three admits fewer tasks, and where to stop depends on what a deployer loses by dropping a frontier judge that was needed, against paying for one that was not;
moreover, with just eight datasets, the calls change only where a threshold crosses a dataset’s own coordinate (hatched region of Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a); Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>).
What holds at every operating point is the direction of the test:
over a grid of shares and correlation bars, and on <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}888" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,888</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}888</annotation></semantics></math> (sub-)panels drawn from the same ten members, the admitted panels are more often within reach of the frontier judge, and more often above their own best member, than the rejected ones (Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>).
Therefore, stackers on admissible tasks are expected to improve on the CV-best member;
no task failing the test shows a clear gain over that member, and on dominant-leader ones, the frontier stays materially ahead (§<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The two coordinates are not, however, equally costly.
The correlation one is free:
two binary verdicts against a common gold label agree exactly when both are equally right or wrong, so the members’ mean pairwise <em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">agreement</em> equals that of their error indicators and needs no gold (only its normalisation into <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> does), and it orders the suite like <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> (Spearman <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=+0.93" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.93</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=+0.93</annotation></semantics></math>).
The competence one has no assumption-free unsupervised counterpart: a Dawid–Skene fit to the same votes (§<a href="#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" title="Comparison with an unsupervised aggregator. ‣ 3.1. The panel against its own naive vote ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>) rates all ten members competent where, e.g., on <span id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span> and <span id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span> none clears <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=0.30</annotation></semantics></math>.
On calibration samples, the regime call is reproduced <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>85.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the time from fifty labelled records and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="91.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>91.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">91.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> from a hundred, the budgets at which the aggregator itself becomes worth fitting, so the diagnostic and the calibration are one purchase, whereas naming the best member from a hundred succeeds only <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="69\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>69</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">69\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the time (Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>).
Notably, the error-correlation is largely inherited from pretraining rather than induced by alignment (Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Base-versus-instruct probe ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>), and on four of the eight datasets our cheap panel still carries more independent votes than <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citeauthor"><a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kohli</a></cite>’s <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite> nine frontier judges reach on any of theirs (Appendix <a href="#A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6" title="Effective independence against a frontier panel. ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4. </span>Standing in for a frontier judge</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now ask what is lost and what is gained by running the panel instead of paying for a frontier judge.
We adopt <span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Claude Sonnet</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite> (<span id="S4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">claude-sonnet-4-6</span>; temperature <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>) as frontier judge, and difference it against the panel item by item under the same paired cluster bootstrap (§<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Metrics and the decision rule. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The quality cost.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Read as eight paired differences (the two rightmost columns of Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>; intervals in Appendix <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Open-judge scaling and cost ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>, Table <a href="#A8.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ Amortised cost and break-even. ‣ Appendix H Open-judge scaling and cost ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>), the substitution offers an improvement on two datasets (one of which is <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">clear</span>) and worsens on the remaining six (three <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unresolved</span> and three clear, one of which is negligible).
The clear improvement is <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span> (<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\kappa=+0.070" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.070</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\kappa=+0.070</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[+0.024,+0.117]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.024</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.117</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[+0.024,+0.117]</annotation></semantics></math>), the set on which <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Sonnet</span> is weakest by far (<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=0.165" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.165</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=0.165</annotation></semantics></math>, the next-weakest being <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.418" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.418</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.418</annotation></semantics></math>), below even the panel’s best single member (Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), a shortfall not ascribable to the prompt frame, the better of the two we ran for <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Sonnet</span> (Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>).
<span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>’s improvement and <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>’s, <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span>’s, and <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>’s worsenings are all unresolved, leaving those four statistically too close to the frontier to claim a result in either direction.
Of the three clear worsenings, <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>’s is too small to matter in deployment (<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\kappa=-0.036" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.036</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\kappa=-0.036</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-0.069,-0.003]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.069</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.003</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-0.069,-0.003]</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e. <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.8</annotation></semantics></math> points of balanced accuracy on a task the panel already scores at <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>86.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86.3</annotation></semantics></math>), leaving only <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> (<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.192</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.192</annotation></semantics></math>) and <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> (<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.151" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.151</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.151</annotation></semantics></math>) materially adverse: precisely the two on which one strong judge already captures the task, so the panel has nothing worth aggregating and a frontier model is simply a better single judge.
The results are comparable when read on <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">bacc</span> (which charges every abstention on the full denominator): the panel gives up <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.9</annotation></semantics></math> points on average (<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="73.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>73.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">73.0</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75.9</annotation></semantics></math>) and at most <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.6</annotation></semantics></math> (<span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>), while gaining <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.5</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span> and <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>.
A frontier judge therefore has to be kept in one regime only: the panel holds a median <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="93\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>93</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">93\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the frontier’s <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> and is clearly and materially behind on two of eight, and the account of §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> names those two as the dominant-leader sets — a reading available from the members themselves, at the same labelling cost the aggregator already requires (Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cost and deployment profile.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Cost and deployment profile. ‣ 4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> prices that deficit against what a deployer would weigh.
The ten members together run at $<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.039" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.039</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.039</annotation></semantics></math> per thousand items against $<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.52</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.52</annotation></semantics></math> for the <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Sonnet</span> <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">api</span>, about <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.55\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.55</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.55\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the price (Appendix <a href="#A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Cost. ‣ Appendix H Open-judge scaling and cost ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a> derives both; Appendix <a href="#A13" title="Appendix M Extended limitations ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">M</span></a> bounds them).
Moreover, the panel runs on premises, so no evaluated text leaves the deployer’s infrastructure and no rate limit or model deprecation enters the evaluation loop, a solution the escalation route cannot offer (Appendix <a href="#A12" title="Appendix L Extended related work ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">L</span></a>).
Inference is not, however, where the panel’s money goes.
The stacker needs in-domain labels, so the break-even is a volume rather than a rate, and how large a volume turns on how many labels the aggregator requires, which we measure at fifty to a hundred labelled records (Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>, Figure <a href="#A3.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ The rule as a family of thresholds. ‣ Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>(b)), the same operating range as the diagnostic of §<a href="#S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" title="The admissibility test. ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>.
Priced at $<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> per label, and two labels to a record on the paired sets, that is an outlay of $<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> to $<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">200</annotation></semantics></math>, which the panel’s cheaper inference repays between some <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="81{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>81,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">81{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> evaluated items — a large yet sustainable volume.</p>

<td id="S4.T2.15.1.14.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><math id="S4.T2.m58" class="ltx_Math" alttext="74.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn mathsize="0.800em">74.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">74.7</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td id="S4.T2.15.1.14.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><math id="S4.T2.m62" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bullet" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.800em">∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bullet</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</table>
</span></div></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="S4.T2.16" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel ltx_parbox ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;"><sup id="S4.T2.16.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S4.T2.16.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:70%;">†</span></sup><span id="S4.T2.16.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">: our rerun under the system’s released weights;
<em id="S4.T2.16.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">—</em>: no data;
<em id="S4.T2.16.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">n/a</em>: scope the judge cannot be run on;
<em id="S4.T2.16.2.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">ungr.</em>: applicability to ungrounded factuality (<math id="S4.T2.m64" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bullet" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bullet</annotation></semantics></math> yes, <math id="S4.T2.m65" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\odot" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\odot</annotation></semantics></math> partly, <math id="S4.T2.m66" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\circ" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∘</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\circ</annotation></semantics></math> no);
<em id="S4.T2.16.2.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">cost</em>: inference per <math id="S4.T2.m67" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> items (<span id="S4.T2.16.2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">api</span> or cloud <span id="S4.T2.16.2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">gpu</span> rates, Appendix <a href="#A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Cost. ‣ Appendix H Open-judge scaling and cost ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>) and one-time outlay on a new domain ($<math id="S4.T2.m68" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> per label);
<sup id="S4.T2.16.2.7" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S4.T2.16.2.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">¶</span></sup>: estimated by comparison.</span></p></div></div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Comparison with the <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> leaderboard.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Four of our eight sets are subsampled from the <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> test split and read in balanced accuracy, the metric that leaderboard reports;
Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a> sets out what licenses reading our numbers beside the published ones, showing an agreement within about one point of balanced accuracy, so gaps under three points are not informative.
On those four, the panel reaches <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="69.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>69.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">69.5</annotation></semantics></math>, drawing level with <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Granite Guardian 3.3</span>  and sitting inside the agreement band of the leaderboard’s top system (<span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Bespoke-MiniCheck-7B</span>, <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="71.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>71.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">71.4</annotation></semantics></math>) and of <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GPT-4o</span>  (<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70.8</annotation></semantics></math>); all this from a field whose best member scores <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="67.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>67.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">67.7</annotation></semantics></math> (average member <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="59.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>59.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">59.6</annotation></semantics></math>).
This is, however, the comparison least favourable to the panel, with specialists being scored on the datasets they were built for: run at their documented operating points across our eight datasets, the ordering materially reverses (Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Cost and deployment profile. ‣ 4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>; per-dataset in Appendix <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Purpose-trained cheap judges off their home benchmark ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a>); and
the strongest specialist we reproduce, <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MiniCheck-Flan-T5-L</span>, scores <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="66.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>66.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">66.6</annotation></semantics></math> against the panel’s <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>72.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72.5</annotation></semantics></math> across the six grounded sets, <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="63.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>63.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">63.1</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>86.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86.3</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> alone, and cannot be evaluated on the full suite as its interface requires a document the two ungrounded sets cannot supply.
The evaluation-tuned judges, which do run everywhere, are weak throughout (<span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Prometheus-2</span>  at <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.4</annotation></semantics></math> over the suite, against our <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="73.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>73.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">73.0</annotation></semantics></math>).
A cheap panel does not beat a trained detector on the detector’s own ground, the two serving different ends: a specialist gives the best quality on the distribution it was trained for, while a generalist panel gives comparable verdicts that keep working if the domain moves and the reference disappears.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Outside <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span>.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Two further benchmarks admit a published comparison once the metric is matched, <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> and <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> being reported in hallucinated-class F1 (Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>, Table <a href="#A6.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Harness calibration. ‣ Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>).
On <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> the stacked panel reaches <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>86.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86.2</annotation></semantics></math>, drawing level with the strongest published open judge (<span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-14B</span>, <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>85.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85.2</annotation></semantics></math>) and with <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GPT-4o-mini</span>  (<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>84.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84.1</annotation></semantics></math>), while resting within two points of the published <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GPT-4o</span>  (<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="87.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>87.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">87.7</annotation></semantics></math>).
Three of the published detectors are <em id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.7" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">members of our own panel</em>, which gives a second harness calibration (Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>).
On <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>, however, the published numbers sit on that corpus’s test split, at a hallucinated rate of <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.178" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.178</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.178</annotation></semantics></math> against the <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> our construction imposes, and hallucinated-class F1 moves with prevalence, so our rows are not comparable in level with them.
The anchors themselves show the pattern of this paper, with the strongest prompt-only system (<span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GPT-4-turbo</span>, <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45.6</annotation></semantics></math>) falling far below the three detectors fine-tuned on the corpus (<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>68.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68.2</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="74.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>74.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">74.8</annotation></semantics></math>).
On <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> prevalence is matched; however, we charge abstentions as missed detections and the two sides are not scored on the same items, so results compare levels and license no ranking.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Open-judge scaling.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Size alone does not close the remaining gap either: a larger <em id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">open</em> judge does not improve monotonically with scale, <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-32B</span>  being the better of the two on four sets, and <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-72B</span>  trails <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Sonnet</span> on four of the eight, drawing level mostly where the frontier is weakest (Appendix <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Open-judge scaling and cost ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>).
Within the one open family we scaled, parameter count is therefore not what separates an open judge from a frontier model.
A single <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-32B</span>  is nonetheless a close rival on average (<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>72.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72.6</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="73.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>73.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">73.0</annotation></semantics></math> suite <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">bacc</span>, Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Cost and deployment profile. ‣ 4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), yet nothing tells a deployer in advance where it will hold, whereas the panel’s regime is read from its own members.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5. </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we studied whether a panel of cheap open-weight judges can stand in for a frontier one, what the substitution sacrifices, and when it is worth making.
We built that panel from ten <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math>B members of uneven and, on any new task, unknown competence:
none of them clears our competence bar on all eight benchmarks, and naming the strongest from a hundred labelled records succeeds only <math id="S5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="69\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>69</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">69\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the time.
Without knowing which to trust, we still read from all ten a verdict at least as good as the best of them, holding a median <math id="S5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="93\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>93</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">93\%</annotation></semantics></math> of <span id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Claude Sonnet</span>’s <math id="S5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> and giving up <math id="S5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.9</annotation></semantics></math> points of balanced accuracy on average, for a sixty-fourth of the inference cost, and with nothing leaving the deployer’s premises.
Out of the eight analysed benchmarks, the panel clearly leads on one and falls materially behind on only two.
The panel’s cost is a one-time in-domain calibration of <math id="S5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> records, amortised against <span id="S5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Sonnet</span> after some <math id="S5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="81" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>81</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">81</annotation></semantics></math>K items.
Against the label-free ways of reading the same votes the gain is unconditional, the panel being clearly ahead of the average member everywhere and never clearly beaten by an unsupervised aggregator;
against its own best member it is not, the panel leading where competence is spread and errors decorrelate, and otherwise recovering its leader.
Both coordinates of that condition are read from the same calibration set the aggregator already consumes, so a deployer can estimate the regime before committing to the panel.
The main limitation is that the panel is capped by its roster: the gain requires several individually capable members whose errors decorrelate, a condition that might drift from roster to roster and from one model version to the next, and one we characterise for a single fixed roster of frozen generalists.
Adding members pays only where they already decorrelate from one another:
since error-correlation rises with model accuracy <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>, <a href="#bib.bib74" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite>, larger members should not be expected to relax that condition, which makes roster composition the lever worth pulling.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Code and data availability</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All code, together with the per-dataset run artefacts from which every result is produced, is available as two GitHub repositories, split where a reader could regenerate everything without intensive or costly computation.<span id="footnote4" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">4</span>
            
            
            
            
            
            
            
          <a href="https://github.com/eOnofri04/raim-verdicts" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/eOnofri04/raim-verdicts</a> and <a href="https://github.com/eOnofri04/raim-analysis" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/eOnofri04/raim-analysis</a>.</span></span></span>
<span id="Sx1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">raim-verdicts</span> carries the full inference pipeline, from dataset construction and prompt rendering to the model backends and the verdict parser, and is readily extensible to further models (mainly via Hugging Face) or benchmarks (mainly via the Python <span id="Sx1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">datasets</span> library);
<span id="Sx1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">raim-analysis</span> carries everything that regenerates from the verdicts, namely the stacked aggregator and cross-fit, the cluster-bootstrap machinery, and the table- and figure-generation pipeline.
The full verdicts, paid <span id="Sx1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">api</span> generations included, are released in <span id="Sx1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">raim-verdicts</span> as well.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Both repositories are released under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
That licence cannot cover the benchmarks, whose terms a <span id="Sx1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">NOTICE</span> file records source by source;
we distribute only our own verdict records, keyed to a content-addressed index against which a third party can verify the join to each publisher’s data without our redistributing any source text.
The decision rule and the bootstrap protocol are specified in §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Metrics and the decision rule. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, the judge prompt, decoding constraints, and coverage accounting in Appendix <a href="#A11" title="Appendix K Judge roster, prompt, and coverage ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">K</span></a>, and the full per-dataset ladders in Appendix <a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Every reported number other than the re-run agreements below is generated programmatically from in-repo artefacts: the <span id="Sx1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">QUICKSTART</span> of <span id="Sx1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">raim-analysis</span> gives the commands that verify the data, rebuild every table and figure from the committed derived tier in minutes, print the headline numbers of the text beside the files they are read from, and regenerate that tier from the plain verdicts within about an hour, with no <span id="Sx1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">gpu</span> and no network, under Python 3.12 to 3.14 on macOS and Linux.
The analysis is deterministic at <span id="Sx1.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">seed</span> <math id="Sx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=0</annotation></semantics></math> on a given machine, whereas across hardware the order in which the numerical libraries accumulate sums perturbs the ninth decimal and beyond;
the release therefore checks a regenerated tier against the committed one at a <math id="Sx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-8}</annotation></semantics></math> tolerance on floating-point values and exactly on counts, labels, judging conditions, and panel membership, so that a number which has really moved fails the check whereas a change of hardware does not.
Inference, conversely, is not bit-reproducible across <span id="Sx1.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">gpu</span> model or serving stack, which is why the verdicts are released as data: a full re-run on independent hardware, with vLLM and <span id="Sx1.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">transformers</span> a major version ahead, moved individual verdicts (median per-judge agreement <math id="Sx1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.98" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.98</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.98</annotation></semantics></math> for the generative panel, <math id="Sx1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.99</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.99</annotation></semantics></math> for the constrained scorer) but left every win/tie verdict of §<a href="#S3" title="3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> unchanged.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="Sx3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Ethics statement</h2>

<div id="Sx3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Sx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This work evaluates existing model outputs and collects no new human-generated data: all eight benchmarks are publicly released datasets with published gold labels, used under their respective licences and terms, and no human subjects or annotators were involved.
We redistribute only derived per-item judge verdicts and aggregate results, never the source datasets, which can be fetched from their publishers (all but <span id="Sx3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> through the Python <span id="Sx3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">datasets</span> module).
The method’s purpose, i.e. detecting unsupported content in generated text, is safety-positive and, being an evaluator rather than a generator, offers little scope for misuse.
One benchmark (<span id="Sx3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>) contains medical question-answering material with synthesised hallucinations; our detector is a research artefact evaluated on that benchmark’s terms and is not a clinical tool.</p>
</div>
</section>
