<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Roadmap to the appendices</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The appendices that follow are organised by topic for navigability, so they do not follow the order in which the main body cites them.
For ease of discoverability, we introduce them briefly here.
Appendices <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>–<a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Transfer to an unseen dataset ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a> extend the account the paper is built on, from the item-level test that supports it to the transfer result that bounds it.
Appendices <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>–<a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Open-judge scaling and cost ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a> carry the comparisons against systems we did not build, and the calibrations that license them.
Appendices <a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>–<a href="#A13" title="Appendix M Extended limitations ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">M</span></a> hold the per-dataset tables, the measurement protocol, and the reference material a reproduction would need.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A1.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Appendix A Roadmap to the appendices ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> maps each appendix to what it carries and to the part of the body it supports, so that any headline in the main text can be traced back to the measurement behind it.
No appendix is required to follow the argument;
each is written to be read on its own, and the body cites it at the point its content is used.</p>
</div>

<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>The competence/correlation account in full</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix carries the account of §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> in full: the two quantitative views of it –an item-level test with real power, and a cross-dataset predictor without it– then the regime ordering read dataset by dataset, the member-level views, the panel-size sweep, and the effective-independence comparison the body only points at.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Item-level recovery test (confirmatory).</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The mechanism predicts that the panel beats the best single by recovering the leader’s errors from decorrelated member competence.
We test this directly: pooling the eight datasets and restricting to the items on which the CV-best single judge is wrong –so that any recovery must come from the other members– we relate the panel’s per-item recovery to the fraction of members individually correct on that item (Table <a href="#A2.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Item-level recovery test (confirmatory). ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>).
The relation is strong and orderly (Table <a href="#A2.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Item-level recovery test (confirmatory). ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>(a)): the panel never recovers an item on which every member shares the leader’s error (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="529" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>529</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">529</annotation></semantics></math> such items), recovers about one in six once two members dissent, and about six in seven where nine of the ten are right.
A logistic regression with dataset fixed effects gives a coefficient of <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+4.67" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>4.67</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+4.67</annotation></semantics></math> (log-odds) on the members-correct fraction, and the correlation between recovery and that fraction –a Pearson correlation between the binary recovery outcome and the continuous fraction, hence a point-biserial one– is <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.41" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.41</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.41</annotation></semantics></math> pooled over the <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}998" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,998</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}998</annotation></semantics></math> items (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&lt;10^{-20}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&lt;10^{-20}</annotation></semantics></math>) and positive within each of the eight datasets, median <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.48</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.48</annotation></semantics></math> (Table <a href="#A2.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Item-level recovery test (confirmatory). ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>(b)).
This test, and not the dataset-level correlation below, carries the mechanism’s quantitative support, for two reasons.
The first is that conditioning on the leader being wrong removes the leader from the test: on these items its verdict is fixed at incorrect, so a relation between recovery and the <em id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">other</em> members’ competence cannot be an echo of how strong the leader is, nor of the selection that made it the leader.
The second is that the unit of analysis is the item, so the estimate rests on nearly two thousand points instead of the eight a dataset-level correlation must rest on — and eight points cannot resolve an effect of this size, as the next paragraph shows.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.T4" class="ltx_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A2.T4.12" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Table 4</span>. </span><span id="A2.T4.13" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Item-level mechanism test on the <math id="A2.T4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}998" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,998</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}998</annotation></semantics></math> items on which the CV-best single judge is wrong.

<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cross-dataset predictor (illustrative only).</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The dataset-level counterpart of that test is reported here for completeness, and is the one quantity in this appendix the paper does not lean on.
The account also makes a prediction across datasets –the panel’s edge should be largest where member errors decorrelate and competence is spread over several members– and it is fair to ask whether the eight datasets bear that out numerically as well as qualitatively.
We form, per dataset, the product of the two quantities the account names: <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> is the mean pairwise error-correlation of the ten members (the quantity Figure <a href="#A2.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Effective independence against a frontier panel. ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> displays in full), and the number of members reaching <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa\geq 0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa\geq 0.30</annotation></semantics></math>, our count of how far competence is spread; these are the two coordinates of the plane in Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a).
Rank-correlating that composite against each dataset’s <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">(stacked <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> best-single)</span> <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> gap gives Spearman <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=+0.47" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.47</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=+0.47</annotation></semantics></math> — the predicted sign, and consistent with the regime ordering read off in §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>, but not significant (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.24</annotation></semantics></math>).
Nor could it easily be, since at <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=8</annotation></semantics></math> only a strong ordering (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho\gtrsim 0.74" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>≳</mo><mn>0.74</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho\gtrsim 0.74</annotation></semantics></math>) would register, and a composite that squeezes two quantities into one number cannot be expected to produce one.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A2.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Cross-dataset predictor (illustrative only). ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> reads the two coordinates separately, which is the more informative view and the less flattering one.
The competence coordinate carries the stronger association in every subset (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.48</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.48</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.74" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.74</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.74</annotation></semantics></math>), and the correlation coordinate the weaker one (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.36" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.36</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.36</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.61" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.61</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.61</annotation></semantics></math>).
Both, however, are sensitive to the obvious check of dropping the sets held back in §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" title="Benchmarks and judges. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, yet most of that sensitivity comes from one dataset.
<span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, in fact, carries the most correlated panel in the suite (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}=0.854" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.854</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}=0.854</annotation></semantics></math>, or an effective <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{eff}}=1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{eff}}=1.15</annotation></semantics></math> independent votes on the scale defined below) together with the third-largest gap (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.051" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.051</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.051</annotation></semantics></math>, behind only <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> and <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>), which is the opposite of what the account predicts.
It is also the set held back for having too few clusters to resolve any paired difference, so that gap is a central estimate whose interval accommodates either sign.
<span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> carried a distortion of another kind, one that re-framing the four <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> sets removed.
Under the misframed prompt none of its members was competent, yet the stacker beat the best single judge by <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.116" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.116</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.116</annotation></semantics></math>, by correcting a miscalibrated leader rather than by pooling complementary competence (Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>);
under the corrected frame, nine of its ten members clear <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=0.30</annotation></semantics></math>.
The re-framing thus removed a confound, though not the lack of power.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">No entry in Table <a href="#A2.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Cross-dataset predictor (illustrative only). ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> reaches significance at <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\leq 8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\leq 8</annotation></semantics></math>.
Read instead against the panel’s <em id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">absolute</em> stacked <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, rather than against its gap over the best single, the two coordinates give <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=-0.76" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.76</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=-0.76</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=+0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=+0.95</annotation></semantics></math> for the member count; both, however, are confounded by how hard the task is, and neither is a statement about the panel’s advantage.
The competence/correlation account does not depend on this reading, its quantitative test being the item-level one of Table <a href="#A2.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Item-level recovery test (confirmatory). ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, over some two thousand points rather than eight.
We therefore read the dataset-level axis qualitatively, through the regime ordering and the plane of Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a).</p>
</div>

<table id="A2.T5.6" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="A2.T5.6.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T5.6.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_border_tt"></td>
<td id="A2.T5.6.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_border_tt"></td>
<td id="A2.T5.6.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" colspan="3"><span id="A2.T5.6.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Spearman <math id="A2.T5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> (two-sided <math id="A2.T5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>) against the <span id="A2.T5.6.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text">(stacked <math id="A2.T5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> best-single)</span> <math id="A2.T5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> gap</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A2.T5.6.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T5.6.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A2.T5.6.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">subset</span></td>

</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The regime ordering by dataset.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The regime ordering that §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> reads off Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a) places the eight datasets in four groups.
The improvement over the best single is largest where competence is distributed over several capable members whose errors decorrelate (<span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span>, <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>);
real but unresolved where the members carry moderate, mutually redundant competence (<span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>);
negligible where one model dominates a weak field and cross-validation reliably finds it (<span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> and <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>, in each of which stacking simply recovers <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Gemma</span>);
and unresolvable either way where competence is scant and the errors are the most correlated in the suite (<span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>).
That ordering carries two qualifications.
The first concerns power rather than effect.
The point gain over the best single is largest on the three least-powered sets, <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.059" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.059</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.059</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=330" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>330</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=330</annotation></semantics></math>), <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.056" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.056</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.056</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=222" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>222</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=222</annotation></semantics></math>), and <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span> (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.051" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.051</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.051</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=114" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>114</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=114</annotation></semantics></math>), all above <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>’s clear <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.032" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.032</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.032</annotation></semantics></math>;
their paired intervals, however, run two to three times wider and cannot exclude zero, so the one resolved win bounds the panel’s advantage from below, and the favourable end of the ordering is under-resolved rather than inactive.
The second concerns the contrast the literature would predict.
Grounded-versus-ungrounded is numerically present in the suite yet mechanistically empty: <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> is the most panel-favourable dataset we measure, whereas <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> is a textbook dominant-leader set whose difference against the best single is indistinguishable from the grounded <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>’s.
The two ungrounded sets thus occupy opposite regimes, and “ungrounded” is not a coherent behavioural category for this question.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Member-level views.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Two member-level figures complete the account, and both are to be read by regime, not member by member.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A2.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Effective independence against a frontier panel. ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> gives the pairwise error-correlation structure of the panel on all eight datasets, ordered by <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the progression across the eight is the axis the account rests on.
On <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}=0.11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.11</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}=0.11</annotation></semantics></math>) the members are close to independent and several pairs are mildly <em id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">anti</em>-correlated, so nearly every member carries information the others lack; by <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.55" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.55</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.55</annotation></semantics></math>) whole blocks of the matrix have gone dark and only a few pairs remain informative; and on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span> (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.85" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.85</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.85</annotation></semantics></math>) the panel is close to one judge repeated ten times, which is why aggregation has so little to exploit there whatever the members’ individual competence.
The figure also shows the two axes of §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> to be distinct: <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> sits at the decorrelated end (<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.26" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.26</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.26</annotation></semantics></math>) and is nonetheless a dominant-leader set whose difference against the best single does not resolve, because only two of its members are individually competent, so low correlation buys nothing without competence to decorrelate.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A2.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ Effective independence against a frontier panel. ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> reads the same regimes member-wise, by refitting the stacker without each member in turn.
Where the panel’s improvement is largest, the profile is flat: on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> no member is worth more than <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.006" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.006</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.006</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> to the panel, and on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> five members each cost <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.03</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.03</annotation></semantics></math> or more, so the gain is jointly held rather than owed to any one judge.
Where a single judge dominates, one cell carries the column: dropping <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Gemma</span> costs <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.066" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.066</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.066</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> and <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.063" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.063</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.063</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>, against at most <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.018" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.018</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.018</annotation></semantics></math> for any other member; on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> it costs <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.062" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.062</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.062</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.036" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.036</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.036</annotation></semantics></math> for the next member, a leader standing out of a competent field rather than dominating a weak one.
The extreme case is <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, where dropping <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Gemma</span> costs <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.158" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.158</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.158</annotation></semantics></math> — by some margin the largest effect in the figure, and a reminder that a <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="114" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>114</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">114</annotation></semantics></math>-item set with the suite’s highest error-correlation is carried by whichever member happens to be competent on it.
No removal helps by more than <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.03</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.03</annotation></semantics></math>, so a blue cell marks a member the panel can spare rather than one it would be better without.
Read as a rule, a flat profile signals distributed competence and predicts the larger improvement over the best single, whereas a single deep notch signals a dominant leader and predicts an unresolved one;
in neither case is the gain the contribution of one strong member alone.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Panel size.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Sweeping the panel from one to ten members corroborates the same ordering directly (Figure <a href="#A3.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ The rule as a family of thresholds. ‣ Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>(a), members added in a greedy decorrelating order and the stacker refitted at each <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>).
Competence keeps accruing with each added member on the low-correlation sets (<span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span>);
the leader-dominated (<span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>, <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>) and the redundant (<span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>) sets stay flat;
and <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> peaks early before diluting.
Aggregation therefore rewards decorrelated competence and not member count, so we read the sweep as a diagnostic and not as a recipe for choosing <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Effective independence against a frontier panel.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The correlation coordinate has a standard summary, which lets us place our panel against one we did not run (§<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>).
Writing <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> for the mean pairwise error-correlation over the <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\binom{k}{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\binom{k}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> member pairs (the correlation coefficient amongst the pairwise diversity measures of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kuncheva and Whitaker [42]</a></cite>, computed on correct/incorrect outputs and hence identical on error indicators), Kish’s effective sample size <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{eff}}=k/(1+(k-1)\,\bar{\phi})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{eff}}=k/(1+(k-1)\,\bar{\phi})</annotation></semantics></math> gives the number of independent judges a panel of <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> correlated ones is worth.
Our ten members are worth <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{eff}}=5.11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5.11</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{eff}}=5.11</annotation></semantics></math> independent votes on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span>, <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.98" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.98</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.98</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>, <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.58" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.58</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.58</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>, <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.49" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.49</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.49</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.84" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.84</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.84</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>, <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.69" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.69</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.69</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>, <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.64</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>, and <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.15</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, which places the correlation axis of the account on a single scale.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kohli [40]</a></cite> evaluates the same <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> statistic for a panel of <em id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.9" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">nine frontier judges</em> on three natural-language-inference (<span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">nli</span>) corpora, reporting <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{eff}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{eff}}</annotation></semantics></math> between <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.18</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.48</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.48</annotation></semantics></math>, with the best single judge unbeaten and an asymptote at <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/\bar{\phi}\approx 2.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/\bar{\phi}\approx 2.6</annotation></semantics></math> read there as a bound on what panels of current models can reach.
No row is shared between the two studies and the tasks differ, so this compares a derived, panel-internal quantity rather than a score;
yet on that quantity our cheap panel exceeds their frontier panel’s best on four of eight datasets and passes the asymptote on two, reaching nearly twice that value on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In concurrent work on preference data, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib67" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hossain et al. [27]</a></cite> claim the same ordering on a shrinkage estimate of <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>, ten open judges being worth <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.5</annotation></semantics></math> independent ones and three frontier judges <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.4</annotation></semantics></math>.
We interpret this as the prediction of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al. [36]</a></cite> and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib74" title="" class="ltx_ref">Goel et al. [20]</a></cite> realised –error-correlation rises with model accuracy, so a panel assembled from weaker and more heterogeneous judges has more independence to aggregate– and recover Kohli’s negative result:
a panel of nine strong, mutually redundant judges sits just above our four least favourable sets on that scale, and on those four we too find aggregation recovers the leader and no more.
It also shows the asymptote to be a property of that roster rather than of panels, since it is <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> that fixes the bound and <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> is a choice of members.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib88" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li and Hai [46]</a></cite> argue the same dependence analytically for committees of language models: under a one-factor model, positively correlated errors leave every rule that reads only the votes a positive error floor however large the committee, and reduce a committee of fixed size to single-member behaviour as the correlation approaches one.
The two axes remain distinct here as elsewhere:
<span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> carries <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{eff}}=2.98" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2.98</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{eff}}=2.98</annotation></semantics></math> and still yields nothing, only two of its members being individually competent.</p>
</div>

<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>The admissibility test and its labelling budget</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix carries the measurement behind §<a href="#S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" title="The admissibility test. ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>: the rule itself, the identity that makes one regime coordinate free, the obstruction that keeps the other from being so, and the budget at which the call stabilises.
Figure <a href="#A3.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ The rule as a family of thresholds. ‣ Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> collects the two budgets a deployer sets by dataset, the panel size of Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> and the calibration size measured here.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The rule.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The test reads two statistics off a labelled calibration sample, both computed from the members’ own verdicts and neither from the stacker’s weights.
The first is the competence spread <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=|\{i\mid\kappa_{i}\geq\kappa_{0}\}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=|\{i\mid\kappa_{i}\geq\kappa_{0}\}|</annotation></semantics></math>, the number of members whose own <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> against gold clears a competence bar <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>;
the second is <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>, the mean over the <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\binom{N_{v}}{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\binom{N_{v}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> member pairs of the Pearson correlation between their error indicators <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="e_{i}=\mathbf{1}[v_{i}\neq y]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{i}=\mathbf{1}[v_{i}\neq y]</annotation></semantics></math>, each pair read on the items both members committed on.
For a competence bar <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, a share <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>, and a correlation bar <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, a task is <em id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">admissible</em> when <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\geq c\,N_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\geq c\,N_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}\leq\phi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}\leq\phi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The numbers we report are those of one instance, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\kappa_{0},c,\phi_{0})=(0.30,\tfrac{1}{2},0.40)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.30</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mn>0.40</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\kappa_{0},c,\phi_{0})=(0.30,\tfrac{1}{2},0.40)</annotation></semantics></math>, declared once and applied unchanged to every dataset and every calibration sample, the competence bar being the one of §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> and Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.
These values were fixed with the eight results in view, yet not tuned: eight datasets are too few for any tuning to be stable, as the next paragraph shows, and the paper therefore relies on what holds across the family rather than on the instance itself.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In use, admissibility decides whether to fit the stacker rather than select a single member, and on this suite every admitted task is also one on which the frontier judge is not materially ahead;
whether the frontier judge is worth keeping on a task that fails it is read, qualitatively, from the same two coordinates, as the dominant-leader corner of the plane (§<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>).
On the full samples the test admits <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> (<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=10</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}=0.335" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.335</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}=0.335</annotation></semantics></math>), <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> (<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.320" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.320</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.320</annotation></semantics></math>), and <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> (<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.106" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.106</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.106</annotation></semantics></math>), and rejects the other five (Table <a href="#A3.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ The budget sweep. ‣ Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>);
the suite’s one clear improvement over the CV-best single, on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, falls inside the admissible set, and no rejected task carries one.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">It is however worth stating that the test itself is a decision heuristic rather than a hypothesis test, and carries no interval of its own.
We measure its reliability below instead, as the probability that a calibration sample of a given size reproduces the full-sample call, and name there its two failure cases, the boundary sets <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> and <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The rule as a family of thresholds.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Two properties of the rule, and not of our data, make its thresholds a choice rather than an estimate.
First, the admissible set is monotone in each threshold: raising <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>, or lowering <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, can only remove tasks from it.
The family therefore runs from a screen that admits every task to one that admits none.
As such, choosing a member of it means choosing an operating point between two errors, i.e. dropping the frontier judge where it was needed or paying for it where it was not.
Their relative cost, consequently, belongs to the deployer, and the data cannot estimate it.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Second, on a finite suite the calls are piecewise constant in the thresholds, changing only where a threshold crosses some dataset’s own coordinate.
Any criterion scored on the suite is therefore optimised by a cell of that partition rather than by a point, and which cell wins is decided by the datasets on its edges.
At <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}=0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}=0.30</annotation></semantics></math>, our instance lies in a cell of the plane spanned by the required count <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> that is L-shaped rather than rectangular (hatched area in Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a)).
The count may run from three to five members and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.335" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.335</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.335</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.494" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.494</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.494</annotation></semantics></math>, the upper limit becoming unbounded at a count of five, since no rejected dataset has five competent members.
Its edges are set by the datasets they touch: <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>’s <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> on the left, <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>’s two competent members below, <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span>’s five above, and <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span> at the inner corner.
The competence bar moves the points of that plane rather than an edge, and with the other two thresholds fixed, the result is unchanged for <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.269\leq\kappa_{0}\leq 0.339" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.269</mn><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.339</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.269\leq\kappa_{0}\leq 0.339</annotation></semantics></math>, between the fifth-ranked members of <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> and <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span>;
no call in the paper changes within either range.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The sub-panels of our ten members show both properties at work.
Each of the <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}888" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,888</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}888</annotation></semantics></math> (sub-)panels we draw on the same items (per dataset, every subset of eight or nine members, sixty drawn of five, six, and seven, and the full ten) has its own two coordinates, which we score with the paper’s stacker against its own CV-best member and against the frontier judge.
We score a threshold pair by Youden’s index <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">79</a>]</cite>, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J=\mathrm{TPR}+\mathrm{TNR}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>TPR</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>TNR</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J=\mathrm{TPR}+\mathrm{TNR}-1</annotation></semantics></math>, the rate at which the test admits the panels that meet a target plus the rate at which it rejects those that do not, less one (equivalently, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\,\textsc{bacc}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">bacc</mtext></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\,\textsc{bacc}-1</annotation></semantics></math> of the call against the target), so that <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J=0</annotation></semantics></math> for a call unrelated to the target and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J=1</annotation></semantics></math> for a perfect one.
Selecting <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> on the panels by <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math>, with the target that the panel stays within <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.10</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> of the frontier judge, gives <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=0.4</annotation></semantics></math> with any <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}\geq 0.53" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.53</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}\geq 0.53</annotation></semantics></math> rather than our instance.
Selected instead on seven datasets and applied to the eighth, the optimum moves from fold to fold (<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.43</annotation></semantics></math> upwards), as the partition predicts, yet it returns our call on all eight held-out datasets, and on seven of eight when the target is to beat the CV-best member.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">What does not move, however and most importantly, is the overall direction.
We scan a grid of <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\in\{0.3,0.4,\dots,0.8\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.4</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\in\{0.3,0.4,\dots,0.8\}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}\in\{0.25,0.26,\dots,0.90\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.26</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0.90</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}\in\{0.25,0.26,\dots,0.90\}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\times 66=396" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>66</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>396</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\times 66=396</annotation></semantics></math> pairs, and keep those that split the panels, admitting some and rejecting others.
At every such pair <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> holds for both targets: the admitted panels are more often within reach of the frontier judge than the rejected ones, and more often above their own best member.
This holds at all <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="396" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>396</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">396</annotation></semantics></math> pairs on the drawn panels, every one of which splits them, and at all <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="375" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>375</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">375</annotation></semantics></math> that split the eight full ones, the other <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>21</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\geq 0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\geq 0.6</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}&lt;0.32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}&lt;0.32</annotation></semantics></math>) admitting none of the eight;
likewise, with the frontier margin tightened to <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.05</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.05</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, it still holds at <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>92</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the pairs on the drawn panels, and at all of them on the full ones.
We therefore offer the test as a family whose every member points the same way, and our instance as one operating point of it.
The sub-panels share members and items, so this is evidence across panel configurations rather than across tasks, and a new task remains the test the suite cannot supply.</p>
</div>
