</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The agreement identity.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We write <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> for member <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>’s verdict on an item carrying gold <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="e_{i}=\mathbf{1}[v_{i}\neq y]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{i}=\mathbf{1}[v_{i}\neq y]</annotation></semantics></math> for its error indicator.
Since <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> is common to the two members being compared, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}=v_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}=v_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> holds exactly when <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{i}=e_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{i}=e_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, so the pairwise agreement <em id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">rate</em> is the same statistic read through either lens, and averaging over the <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45</annotation></semantics></math> member pairs preserves the equality.
Member disagreement is therefore an observable proxy for error-decorrelation.
The identity is not new: it is the pairwise case of the agreement equations from which <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">Platanios et al. [61]</a></cite> estimate classifiers’ error rates without labels, each agreement rate being written through the two members’ error rates and their joint one, whereas we use it only to make the correlation coordinate observable.
The Pearson <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> of Figure <a href="#A2.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Effective independence against a frontier panel. ‣ Appendix B The competence/correlation account in full ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> is the same agreement centred and scaled by the members’ error rates, and it is that normalisation, not the association, which consumes gold; the unnormalised rate ranks the eight datasets as <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> does at Spearman <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=+0.93" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.93</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=+0.93</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.001</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The competence obstruction.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The natural candidate is the Dawid–Skene fit already used as an aggregator baseline (§<a href="#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" title="Comparison with an unsupervised aggregator. ‣ 3.1. The panel against its own naive vote ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>), which estimates each member’s reliability by expectation-maximisation without gold.
It fails here for a structural reason.
Its estimate is a member’s agreement with a latent consensus, and where the panel shares an error the consensus is the error: on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, the suite’s most correlated panel, it rates all ten members competent at <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa\geq 0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa\geq 0.30</annotation></semantics></math> against the consensus, whereas not one of them clears that bar against gold, and the same happens on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>.
Across the eight datasets its count of competent members rank-correlates with the gold count at <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=-0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.01</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=-0.01</annotation></semantics></math>, and it recovers the true best member on three datasets of eight — failing, in particular, on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>, the suite’s clearest dominant-leader set.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib73" title="" class="ltx_ref">Balasubramanian et al. [4]</a></cite> claim a complementary failure on the aggregation side:
on correlated judges, an aggregator that assumes conditional independence can be confidently wrong even when handed each judge’s true accuracy and, under some dependence structures, it stays strictly suboptimal however large the panel grows.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Nor does a richer label-free model escape the obstruction without an assumption.
The agreement rates of all subsets of the <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> members supply <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{N_{v}}-N_{v}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msup><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{N_{v}}-N_{v}-1</annotation></semantics></math> equations for the <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{N_{v}}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{N_{v}}-1</annotation></semantics></math> individual and joint error rates, short by exactly the <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> individual ones <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">61</a>]</cite>, so every such estimator closes the system by an assumption on how the errors depend on one another –conditional independence for Dawid–Skene, the least dependence the agreements allow for <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citeauthor"><a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">Platanios et al.</a></cite>, independence between groups of dependent members for <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib81" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jaffe et al. [30]</a></cite>– and by members better than chance.
A panel whose errors load on one shared source and whose average member sits near chance, as on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span> (<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=0.088" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.088</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=0.088</annotation></semantics></math>), is hence precisely where those assumptions fail.
An unlabelled sample can say that a panel agrees with itself; it cannot say whether the panel is right.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The budget sweep.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each dataset and each budget <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in\{10,25,50,100,200\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in\{10,25,50,100,200\}</annotation></semantics></math> not exceeding the dataset, we draw <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=200</annotation></semantics></math> calibration samples and recompute both coordinates and the panel’s apparent leader on each.
Sampling is by cluster and truncated at the cluster boundary, matching the resampling unit of §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Metrics and the decision rule. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>: a deployer buys labelled records, and taking half a matched pair would give the sample a class balance the labelled set would not have.
Table <a href="#A3.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ The budget sweep. ‣ Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> reports how often the full-sample regime call is reproduced: on average <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>85.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the time from fifty labelled records and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="91.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>91.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">91.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> from a hundred, with <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> itself recovered to within a median <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.022" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.022</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.022</annotation></semantics></math> at the latter.
Two datasets sit at the decision boundary and are correspondingly unstable, <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> carrying the five competent members the rule requires and no more, and <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>’s members clustering at <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=0.30</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">One property of the rule at our instance should be stated plainly.
There, the correlation bar is not what rejects any dataset.
Every dataset with at least five competent members also satisfies <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}\leq 0.40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.40</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}\leq 0.40</annotation></semantics></math>, and every dataset above the bar has already failed the count, so at the instance the call coincides with the competence threshold alone on all eight.
This is a property of eight points rather than of the rule.
The bar binds from below, since a value under <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>’s <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.335" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.335</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.335</annotation></semantics></math> would reject it, and at a share of three or four members it is the bar alone that rejects <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>;
what the suite lacks at our share is a dataset with five competent members and strongly shared errors, which is why the hatched region of Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a) runs unbounded at a count of five.
We therefore report the conjunction as the account requires it, noting that the eight full panels do not test its correlation half at our instance.
The sub-panels do populate that cell: <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="106" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>106</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">106</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="680" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>680</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">680</annotation></semantics></math> with enough competent members exceed the correlation bar, on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>, and <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>, and on the two datasets where both sides of the bar occur the more correlated ones gain less over their best member (<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.030" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.030</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.030</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.038" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.038</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.038</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.035" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.035</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.035</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.023" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.023</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.023</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>), the direction the correlation half predicts, although on two datasets only.
The optimum above is flat for every <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{0}\geq 0.53" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.53</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{0}\geq 0.53</annotation></semantics></math> for the same reason: at <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=0.4</annotation></semantics></math> no drawn panel with enough competent members lies above that value.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The instability of the two boundary sets belongs to the threshold and not to the estimate: replacing the count by the continuous competence the panel carries above the bar, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{i}\max(0,\kappa_{i}-0.30)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{i}\max(0,\kappa_{i}-0.30)</annotation></semantics></math>, and normalising each statistic by its own spread across the eight datasets, the continuous form resolves about twice as finely at a fifty-record budget (<math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.055" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.055</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.055</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.100</annotation></semantics></math>).
We keep the count in the regime plane of Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a), where it is read qualitatively and its interpretability is worth more than its efficiency, and report the continuous companion in the released artefact.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T6" class="ltx_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A3.T6.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Table 6</span>. </span><span id="A3.T6.9" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Recovery of the regime call from a limited labelling budget. <section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The aggregator’s own budget.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The sweep above prices the <em id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">diagnostic</em>; the aggregator has a budget of its own, and the two are measured the same way.
Table <a href="#A3.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ The aggregator’s own budget. ‣ Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> fits the stacker on <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> labelled records and scores it out-of-fold, against the best single member selected on those same records and the label-free majority vote.
Three design points matter for reading it.
Budgets are in labelled <em id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">records</em>, the clustering unit of §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Metrics and the decision rule. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, which on the paired sets is two items; a deployer buys records, not items.
The folds are the reported stacker’s own, and within each fold the budget is drawn from that fold’s training clusters, the fit predicts that fold’s test items, and the predictions are pooled before <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> is taken — so the estimator is the paper’s, and at the full training pool the curve reproduces the reported value to within <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.003" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.003</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.003</annotation></semantics></math>, which is the check that the protocol has not drifted.
Averaging per-fold <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, instead, would be a different and biased estimator, <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> not being linear in the confusion counts, and disagrees with the pooled one at the full pool by up to <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.010" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.010</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.010</annotation></semantics></math>, on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, whose training pool is the smallest.
The label-free majority vote is drawn on the same folds as a dotted floor per dataset, because what a deployer needs to know is whether the labels they can afford beat spending none.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Two readings the body compresses are clearer per dataset.
The budget at which the fitted stacker overtakes that vote runs from ten labelled records (<span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>, <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>) through twenty-five (<span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>, <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>) to fifty (<span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>, <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>), and on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> not until its full pool of <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="132" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>132</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">132</annotation></semantics></math> — the vote there being within <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.018" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.018</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.018</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> of full supervision, so there is little for labels to buy.
<span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span> is the one set that keeps paying throughout, rising from <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=0.069" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.069</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=0.069</annotation></semantics></math> at ten records to <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.235" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.235</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.235</annotation></semantics></math> at its full pool of <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}088" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,088</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}088</annotation></semantics></math>.
That ordering is not the regime ordering of §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>: the sets on which a handful of labels already pays are the rejected <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> and <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, and the admissible <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> is the slowest, its free vote being already within reach of full supervision.
The two alternatives are not nested, and neither dominates the other.
The free vote is the harder bar on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> and <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> at every budget, on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> below fifty records and on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span> below a hundred;
everywhere else, including on <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.17" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> and <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span> once their thresholds are passed, the harder bar is the best member selected on the same labels.
This is why Figure <a href="#A3.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ The rule as a family of thresholds. ‣ Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>(b) encodes the two on separate channels rather than on one ordinal scale.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The two headline budgets quoted in the body summarise that table, and each has its own exceptions.
Fifty labelled records suffice to clear the label-free vote on seven of the eight datasets, <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> excepted for the reason above;
and a hundred bring the stacker within <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\%</annotation></semantics></math> of its fully supervised <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> on six of the eight, the exceptions being <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>, which is still <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25\%</annotation></semantics></math> short at that budget and keeps paying to its full pool, and <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, whose training pool is too small for the hundred-record point to exist.
Below the crossing point a calibration set is worse than none: at ten labelled records the fitted stacker sits <em id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">beneath</em> the free vote on six of the eight sets, all but <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> and <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, so a deployer who cannot reach the crossing is better served by not fitting an aggregator at all.</p>
</div>

<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Base-versus-instruct probe</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix gives the procedure behind the finding of §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> on where the panel’s error-correlation comes from.
To separate a shared answer-bias from shared task-difficulty as the source of the panel’s error-correlation, we re-run the eight panel families that release a public base (pre-instruction-tuning) checkpoint, i.e. all members except <span id="A4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Phi</span> and <span id="A4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Command-R</span>, which ship only in aligned form.
Each is run in both its base and its instruction-tuned variant under a matched constrained-decoding scorer, holding the underlying models fixed.
For each variant we compute the within-panel mean pairwise error-correlation (<math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>, Pearson on per-item error indicators) across all eight datasets; the two distributions are plotted in Figure <a href="#A4.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix D Base-versus-instruct probe ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>.
The shift <math id="A4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\phi</annotation></semantics></math> (instruct<math id="A4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>base) is negative on seven of the eight datasets, ranging from <math id="A4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.085" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.085</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.085</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> to <math id="A4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.495" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.495</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.495</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span>, and null on <span id="A4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> (<math id="A4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.018" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.018</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.018</annotation></semantics></math>, interval including zero); the base panel’s <math id="A4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> reaches <math id="A4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.667" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.667</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.667</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>.
Excluding from both panels the one instruct member that collapses to a single class under the constrained scorer (<span id="A4.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Falcon</span>), the shift remains clearly negative on six of the eight datasets, <span id="A4.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>’s becoming unresolved (<math id="A4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.027" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.027</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.027</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-0.021,+0.073]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.021</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.073</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-0.021,+0.073]</annotation></semantics></math>) and <span id="A4.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>’s small positive shift resolving (<math id="A4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.046" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.046</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.046</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[+0.023,+0.067]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.023</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.067</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[+0.023,+0.067]</annotation></semantics></math>).
Instruction tuning thus lowers the panel’s error-correlation rather than raising it: the correlation the aligned panel carries is already present, and larger, in the base checkpoints, which is the sense in which §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> reads it as inherited from pretraining rather than induced by alignment.
Being computed on eight members under constrained decoding, the probe’s <math id="A4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> is not the ten-member <math id="A4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> of Table <a href="#A3.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ The budget sweep. ‣ Appendix C The admissibility test and its labelling budget ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, and only its shift is read here.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F7" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.39229v1/fig_baseprobe.svg" id="A4.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/259;" width="476" height="259"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A4.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>. </span><span id="A4.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Within-panel pairwise error-correlation <math id="A4.F7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> (the 28 member pairs) for the matched base and instruct panels, per dataset (each dataset under its own scoring frame, §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" title="Benchmarks and judges. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>; constrained decoding).
The shift <math id="A4.F7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\phi</annotation></semantics></math> (instruct<math id="A4.F7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>base) is summarised in Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Base-versus-instruct probe ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Transfer to an unseen dataset</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The in-domain gain raises the deployment question directly: can a panel calibrated on some datasets be deployed on another without fresh labels?
It cannot, unchanged, and this appendix gives the measurement, the mechanism, and the boundary of the negative.
The conclusion we draw from it is a scope condition on §<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>’s costing –the calibration budget is per domain– rather than a result we develop further.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Measurement and mechanism.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We test with a pooled stacker under a leave-one-dataset-out (<span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">lodo</span>) protocol on the four core grounded sets, fitting on the other three and evaluating on the held-out set (Figure <a href="#A5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Measurement and mechanism. ‣ Appendix E Transfer to an unseen dataset ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>).
Off-domain, the panel returns to roughly the level of the label-free baselines and wins nothing: zero of four transfer wins, with a significant transfer cost –the paired <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text">(in-domain <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> transferred)</span> gap– on the two question-answering sets, <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> (<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.111" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.111</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.111</annotation></semantics></math>) and <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> (<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.175" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.175</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.175</annotation></semantics></math>).
<span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>’s clean win is lost –the transferred stacker drops below even the best single (<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.079" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.079</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.079</annotation></semantics></math>)– and <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>’s unresolved in-domain improvement becomes an outright transfer loss (<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.165" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.165</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.165</annotation></semantics></math>).
On <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> and <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span> the transferred stacker shows no clear transfer cost and does not fall below the best single, though the sample cannot rule out a cost there either.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The mechanism is the one that explains the in-domain pattern: the pooled stacker learns to trust the members that are reliable <em id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">on average</em> over the training pool, but the most reliable judge changes by dataset, so the fixed off-domain weight vector systematically under-weights the held-out set’s specific leader.
On <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> the in-domain leader is <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Granite</span>, yet the off-domain fit gives <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Granite</span> little weight against <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Gemma</span>, so the transferred stacker lands even below <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>’s own best-on-average single.
The apparent <span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> balanced-accuracy gain on transfer is a coverage artefact: it beats only the abstaining CV-best baseline, and loses to the non-abstaining label-free baselines.
The negative therefore reinforces the mechanistic account of §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>:
the panel helps by dataset-specific competence re-weighting, and a fixed weight vector is what that mechanism predicts should fail.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F8" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.39229v1/fig_transfer_narrow.svg" id="A5.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/136;" width="381" height="136"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>. </span><span id="A5.F8.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Leave-one-dataset-out transfer on the four core grounded sets: in-domain stacked and transferred (<span id="A5.F8.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">lodo</span>), against the CV-best single judge and the average member per dataset.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scope of the negative result.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The measurement above is taken in one setting, and the scope matters for what may be concluded from it.
That setting is the generative panel, read through hard verdicts, with a stacker pooled over the other three datasets.
It says that a weight vector fitted on other domains does not carry the in-domain gain, and it identifies why — the leader moves, and a fixed vector cannot follow it.
It does not say that no panel transfers.
In particular, the members are read here through the interface a closed judge would also expose, a verdict rather than a graded confidence, so whether a panel whose members are put on a common scale across domains transfers better is a question this setting cannot reach and we do not take up.
We accordingly take the conservative reading, that the calibration budget of §<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> is per domain, and leave a calibrated-panel transfer study to future work.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Comparability with published results</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The comparison of §<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> against the published results needs three things to be legitimate: a shared set of rows, a shared metric, and evidence that our harness and the leaderboard’s measure the same thing on them.
This appendix supplies all three, states what the comparison cannot reach, and reports the two sets whose published anchors exist but sit on a different denominator.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Shared rows and metric conversion.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Four of our grounded sets (<span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>, <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>, <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>) are drawn from the test split of the <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">73</a>]</cite>, whose public leaderboard<span id="footnote5" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">5</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            <a href="https://llm-aggrefact.github.io/" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://llm-aggrefact.github.io/</a>, retrieved 2026-07-08.</span></span></span> reports balanced accuracy per dataset, so published methods and ours are scored on the same underlying rows.
On a class-balanced set, the chance-agreement term of Cohen’s <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> is exactly <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> whatever the judge’s marginal, so for a full-coverage judge <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=2\,\textsc{bacc}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">bacc</mtext></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=2\,\textsc{bacc}-1</annotation></semantics></math> holds as an identity, not an approximation; abstention perturbs it only through the committed-set treatment of Appendix <a href="#A11" title="Appendix K Judge roster, prompt, and coverage ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">K</span></a>.
Our class balancing subsamples the majority class, which leaves the expected per-class recall –hence balanced accuracy– unchanged, so a published <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">bacc</span> is comparable to ours in expectation; F1 and precision are prevalence-bound and are, conversely, not.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Harness calibration.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A shared metric on shared rows still leaves the two harnesses free to disagree, so Table <a href="#A6.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ Harness calibration. ‣ Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> carries two systems run on both sides.
Re-running <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MiniCheck-Flan-T5-L</span>  through the official MiniCheck package on our instances gives <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>68.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68.4</annotation></semantics></math> mean balanced accuracy against its published <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>68.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68.8</annotation></semantics></math>, and re-running <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-72B</span>  through our own prompting harness gives <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70.4</annotation></semantics></math> against a published <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="69.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>69.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">69.2</annotation></semantics></math> for the unquantised model.
Both agree to about a point, in opposite directions, which is the resolution at which we read the table: differences under three points between blocks are not informative.
A second and independent calibration comes from <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, where three of the published detectors are members of our own panel (§<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>): our runs of them agree with their published hallucinated-class F1 to within <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.6</annotation></semantics></math> points, on a different benchmark and in a different metric from the two rows above.
The exception is <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Bespoke-MiniCheck-7B</span>, which we do not reproduce (<math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>58.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58.3</annotation></semantics></math> against a published <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="71.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>71.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">71.4</annotation></semantics></math>) and whose published row we therefore read instead of ours: its package scores that checkpoint through a generated-token probability rather than through the classifier head its <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Flan-T5</span>  sibling uses, and the loss shows as a drop in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (<span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">auc-roc</span>) on the very same items, so we attribute it to that scoring path rather than to our protocol and do not pursue it here.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T8" class="ltx_table">

<sup id="A6.T8.11.2.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.T8.11.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">§</span></sup>: a checkpoint we do not reproduce (<math id="A6.T8.m86" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>58.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58.3</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A6.T8.m87" class="ltx_Math" alttext="71.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>71.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">71.4</annotation></semantics></math> published), whose published row we read instead (Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>).</span></p></div></div>

<figure id="A6.T9" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A6.T9.25" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Table 9</span>. </span><span id="A6.T9.26" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Hallucinated-class F1 on <span id="A6.T9.26.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> and <span id="A6.T9.26.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>, published and measured here.
Published rows are transcribed from the cited papers (<span id="A6.T9.26.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>: response-level F1 on its QA subtask, which we adopt); ours are computed on our balanced construction (Appendix <a href="#A10" title="Appendix J Dataset construction ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">J</span></a>), an abstention counting as a missed detection.
Slices differ: <span id="A6.T9.26.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>’s published table pools the <math id="A6.T9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>-pair superset against our <math id="A6.T9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>-row <span id="A6.T9.26.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pqa_labeled</span>  slice, and <span id="A6.T9.26.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>’s sits on its QA test split, at a hallucinated rate of <math id="A6.T9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.178" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.178</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.178</annotation></semantics></math> against our <math id="A6.T9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, so its two blocks are not comparable in level, F1 moving with prevalence.
Three published <span id="A6.T9.26.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> detectors are members of our panel (§<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>).</span></figcaption>

</section>
<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The other four benchmarks.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Published work reports on the remaining four benchmarks too, and we record where the field stands on them: on <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> Table <a href="#A6.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Harness calibration. ‣ Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> matches the metric and compares levels, and on <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> it matches the metric but not the prevalence, whereas on <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> and <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> no published number is a baseline we could be scored against.
Tables <a href="#A6.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Harness calibration. ‣ Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> and <a href="#A6.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ The other four benchmarks. ‣ Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> give the strongest anchor we found per set, the metric its authors report, and the structural difference that separates it from ours.
However, the difference changes from set to set, and is never a matter of prompting alone.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">On <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> the published detection table pools the full <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>-pair superset and reports hallucinated-class F1, whereas we use the <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>-row <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pqa_labeled</span>  slice <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">59</a>]</cite>;
the levels nonetheless line up, <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GPT-4o</span>’s <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="87.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>87.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">87.7</annotation></semantics></math> with knowledge against our <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Sonnet</span>’s <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>89.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.0</annotation></semantics></math> and our panel’s <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>86.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86.2</annotation></semantics></math> in the same metric, and three of the detectors reported individually there (<span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-7B</span>  at <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="83.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>83.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">83.9</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Gemma-2-9B</span>  at <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="83.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>83.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">83.8</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Llama-3.1-8B</span>  at <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="79.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>79.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">79.7</annotation></semantics></math>) are members of our own panel, so a reader can compare the two tables member by member.
On <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> every strong published detector is trained on that corpus’s own training split and scored on its original test split at its own prevalence, whereas ours is a paired, balanced construction from the processed corpus’s training split <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">58</a>, <a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">69</a>, <a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite>.
That test split runs at a hallucinated rate of <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.178" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.178</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.178</annotation></semantics></math> against our <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, and F1 moves with prevalence, so Table <a href="#A6.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Harness calibration. ‣ Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> sets the two side by side without ranking them.
Read on the question-answering (QA) subtask we take, the prompt-only anchors there are far weaker (<span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GPT-4-turbo</span>  at F1 <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45.6</annotation></semantics></math>) than the trained ones (<span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">RAG-HAT</span>  at <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="74.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>74.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">74.8</annotation></semantics></math>), which is the in-domain-supervision axis of this paper appearing in someone else’s numbers.
On <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> the canonical automated judge is fine-tuned on in-domain human ratings of <em id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.12" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">model generations</em> and reaches <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>96</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96\%</annotation></semantics></math> validation accuracy on that task, whereas we score the dataset’s own reference answers zero-shot <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">50</a>]</cite>.
Finally, on <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> the published estimators are retrieval-augmented by construction, approximating the human score to within <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\%</annotation></semantics></math> at corpus level, whereas we supply no evidence by design <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">55</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Read together, the four make one point, and it is the paper’s own.
Wherever a published system clearly leads us, it has either been trained on the target corpus or been given evidence we withhold, and the prompted frontier anchor on <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> lands where our frontier judge lands.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">A last caveat covers all eight sets: every published number arrives under its own prompting and inference protocol, and factuality-metric comparisons are known to be fragile to exactly such differences <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite>.
Our absolute levels embed one frame per dataset (<span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">def_on</span>, or the claim-support frame on the <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> sets), applied uniformly to all ten members and the frontier judge (§<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" title="Benchmarks and judges. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), which the within-suite contrasts control for but cross-paper comparisons do not.</p>
</div>

<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Summary of the comparison.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Two readings survive the caveats, beyond the placement recorded in §<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.
<span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>’s low-headroom status is corroborated externally: the leaderboard’s best sits at a <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">bacc</span> of <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.9</annotation></semantics></math> across everything up to <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Claude-3.5</span>  and <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Llama-405B</span>, and our panel reaches that ceiling (<math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="61.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>61.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">61.8</annotation></semantics></math>) without beating its own best single, so the low-headroom verdict of §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" title="Benchmarks and judges. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> is a property of the dataset rather than of our panel.
An independent audit is consistent with this, finding <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span> the most ambiguous of our four <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> sets (<math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> sampled items; <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib82" title="" class="ltx_ref">67</a>]</cite>).
The second reading, that the sharpest competitor to a cheap panel is a small trained verifier rather than another panel, is taken up in the body (§<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>) and not repeated here.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Provenance of the claim-support frame.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The four <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> sets set the item’s question equal to its candidate (the unit judged is one claim against a document), so an initial question–answer rubric (<span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">def_on</span>) presented that claim twice and misframed a claim-verification task; we discovered this by comparing our absolute agreement to the leaderboard, where the unweighted <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">def_on</span> panel sat some twenty balanced-accuracy points below the best published result on those four sets.
We therefore score these four under a MiniCheck-style claim-support frame (§<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" title="Benchmarks and judges. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), which lifts the unweighted panel by <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.7</annotation></semantics></math> of those points on average (Table <a href="#A6.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ Provenance of the claim-support frame. ‣ Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>): on <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span> the frontier judge moves from <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=0.269" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.269</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=0.269</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.418" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.418</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.418</annotation></semantics></math> (<span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">bacc</span> <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="63.5\to 70.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>63.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>70.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">63.5\to 70.9</annotation></semantics></math>), and the panel and all ten members rise in step, bringing the stacked panel to within about a point of the published range on every claim-verification set (Table <a href="#A6.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ Harness calibration. ‣ Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>).
The frontier judge is never worse off for the change either, its <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> rising on all four sets (Table <a href="#A6.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ Provenance of the claim-support frame. ‣ Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>, third block), <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span> included (<math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.137\to 0.165" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.137</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0.165</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.137\to 0.165</annotation></semantics></math>), so the frame each set is scored under is the better of the two for the judge the panel is compared with, and not only for the panel.
The two frames sit on opposite sides of the operating point.
Under the lenient question–answer frame the frontier judge catches only <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="39\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>39</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the hallucinated <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span> items, and under the claim-support frame <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
The shift is therefore one of task scaffolding, not of the judge’s ability to read the evidence.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The two frames double as a controlled manipulation of member competence, and the competence/correlation account of §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> predicts what each should do.
Under the misframed <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">def_on</span> prompt, member competence collapsed to the floor on all four sets (no member reached <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=0.30</annotation></semantics></math> on any of them; Table <a href="#A6.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ Provenance of the claim-support frame. ‣ Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>).
However, the account predicts that a stacker facing crippled, heterogeneously miscalibrated members has the <em id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">most</em> to gain over any single one.
Indeed, the (stacked <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> best-single) edge was larger under that frame, on three of the four sets and on average (<math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.057" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.057</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.057</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.035" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.035</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.035</annotation></semantics></math>).
On <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> it reached a significant win (<math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.116" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.116</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.116</annotation></semantics></math>), which on inspection was the stacker correcting the leader’s frame-induced miscalibration rather than harnessing complementary competence.
However, restoring the frame restores member competence (nine of ten members above <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=0.30</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>), and the edge reverts to the unresolved improvement of §<a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2. The panel against the best single judge ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> (<math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.056" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.056</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.056</annotation></semantics></math>), a competent field also making its best single strong.
The misframing is thus an unplanned natural experiment.
Under a degraded prompt the panel’s advantage inflates as the members are crippled and made heterogeneous, and shrinks as restored competence lifts the best single with them, as the mechanism says it should.
This is evidence for the account independent of the within-frame cross-dataset pattern and of the item-level test.</p>
