<p id="A6.T11.15" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel ltx_parbox ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;"><em id="A6.T11.15.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:70%;">claim</em><span id="A6.T11.15.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">: claim-support frame. <math id="A6.T11.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>: paired difference (claim <math id="A6.T11.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A6.T11.15.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">def_on</span>) with its 95% cluster-bootstrap interval, the same resample applied to both arms.</span></p></div></div>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Purpose-trained cheap judges off their home benchmark</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The competing route to a cheap judge fine-tunes a single small model expressly for evaluation, instead of aggregating a panel of off-the-shelf generalists after the fact (Appendix <a href="#A12" title="Appendix L Extended related work ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">L</span></a>).
It is the natural single-judge foil to the panel, and the published results report it almost exclusively on <span id="A7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span>, which is the corpus family the strongest of these systems were trained for.
We therefore run them ourselves across the whole suite, which is what licenses the scope reading of §<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Cost and deployment profile. ‣ 4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Two families enter.
The grounded-factuality specialists <span id="A7.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MiniCheck-Flan-T5-L</span>  and <span id="A7.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Bespoke-MiniCheck-7B</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">73</a>]</cite> are run through the official MiniCheck inference package rather than our judge-prompt harness, so their published operating point is preserved; they verify a claim against a document and so apply to the six grounded sets alone.
The evaluation-tuned judges <span id="A7.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Prometheus-2</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite>, <span id="A7.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">JudgeLM</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">88</a>]</cite>, and <span id="A7.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Auto-J</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">48</a>]</cite> are run over the same balanced binary instances through a per-judge adapter that renders each instance in the judge’s <em id="A7.p2.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">native</em> graded interface (<span id="A7.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Prometheus-2</span>’s <math id="A7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> absolute-grading rubric, <span id="A7.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">JudgeLM</span>’s and <span id="A7.p2.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Auto-J</span>’s <math id="A7.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A7.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> single-answer scores) and parses the native output back to our label space, thresholding at the scale midpoint.
The reference slot of the graded template carries a rubric describing the ideal faithful answer, never the gold label, so no answer leaks; the source evidence is placed in the instruction exactly as the panel sees it.
Scoring is identical to every other judge in the study: the same instances, non-answers charged through coverage, and the same <math id="A7.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=2000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=2000</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A7.p2.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">row_id</span> cluster bootstrap.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Three caveats bound the reading, and each, if anything, understates the comparators.
The evaluation-tuned three were trained predominantly for general response quality or pairwise preference rather than reference-grounded faithfulness, so we read them as off-the-shelf single-judge baselines and not as faithfulness specialists; <span id="A7.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">JudgeLM</span>  in particular is natively pairwise and is run through its single-answer grading path.
The midpoint threshold is a documented default and not a tuned operating point, so these numbers are a floor a dev-split calibration could only raise.
Finally, their context windows differ by architecture: only <span id="A7.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Prometheus-2</span>  (built on a <math id="A7.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>k-context <span id="A7.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Mistral</span>) reaches the <math id="A7.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8192</annotation></semantics></math>-token window the panel and the frontier judge use, whereas <span id="A7.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Auto-J</span>  (<span id="A7.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Llama-2</span>, <math id="A7.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4096</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4096</annotation></semantics></math>) and <span id="A7.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">JudgeLM</span>  (<span id="A7.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Vicuna</span>/<span id="A7.p3.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Llama-1</span>, <math id="A7.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2048</annotation></semantics></math>) are architecturally capped below it, so on the long-document sets they see middle-out-truncated evidence — a property of the checkpoint and not a design choice, which can only depress their scores.
None of the three bears on the specialist comparison that carries the scope argument, since <span id="A7.p3.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MiniCheck-Flan-T5-L</span>  is run at its own published operating point through its own package and reproduces its published <span id="A7.p3.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> value to within a point (Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>).
Table <a href="#A7.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ On the applicability of Granite Guardian. ‣ Appendix G Purpose-trained cheap judges off their home benchmark ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> gives all five judges’ Cohen’s <math id="A7.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> per dataset, beside the stacked panel, its best single member, and the frontier judge; coverage runs from <math id="A7.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.892" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.892</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.892</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A7.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.000</annotation></semantics></math> across every purpose-trained judge/dataset cell, so none of these rows is decided by a parsing failure.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">On the applicability of <span id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Granite Guardian</span>.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Granite Guardian 3.3</span>  is the one comparator in Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Cost and deployment profile. ‣ 4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> marked only <em id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">partly</em> applicable to ungrounded factuality, and the qualification is worth spelling out, since it is what separates that row from the two <span id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MiniCheck</span>  rows above it.
It is a multi-risk guardrail model and not a faithfulness verifier, and much of what it detects needs no reference at all: jailbreak attempts, profanity, toxicity, hate speech, and the harm dimensions of the IBM AI Risk Atlas are scored from the prompt and the response alone.
It can therefore be pointed at <span id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> and <span id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>, which supply no reference at scoring time (§<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" title="Benchmarks and judges. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), where the <span id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">MiniCheck</span>  interface cannot be run at all.
It cannot, however, deliver there the faithfulness judgement we measure.
Of the risks it defines, only context relevance, groundedness, and answer relevance concern hallucination, and each is scored against a retrieved context, so on an ungrounded item the detector that would carry the faithfulness judgement has nothing to condition on.
The <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\odot" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\odot</annotation></semantics></math> mark records this split, the model running on ungrounded data whilst its faithfulness judgement does not carry over.
We give the row no citation: the family’s technical report documents version 3.0, reports no <span id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> result, and has not been revised since December 2024, so both the results and the version we quote come from the leaderboard.
Nor would its successor change the row: the model card of <span id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Granite Guardian 4.1</span> <span id="footnote6" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">6</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">6</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">6</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            <a href="https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-guardian-4.1-8b" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-guardian-4.1-8b</a>, retrieved 2026-09-25.</span></span></span>, which is not on the leaderboard, gives per-dataset results whose mean over our four sets is <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>68.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68.7</annotation></semantics></math> without and <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>68.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68.6</annotation></semantics></math> with its reasoning mode, against <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="69.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>69.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">69.5</annotation></semantics></math> for version 3.3 with reasoning on the same card.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A7.T12" class="ltx_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 12. </span>Purpose-trained cheap judges off their home benchmark, against the panel and the frontier judge: Cohen’s <math id="A7.T12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> on identical balanced instances, each dataset under its own scoring frame (claim-support on the <span id="A7.T12.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> sets).

<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Open-judge scaling and cost</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix carries the two quantities behind §<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> that the body states: what a larger <em id="A8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">open</em> judge buys, and what each tier costs.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scaling.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To test whether the panel–frontier gap closes with scale alone, we run the single open judges <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-32B</span>  and <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-72B</span>  (4-bit activation-aware weight quantisation, <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">awq</span>, greedy decoding, <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8192</annotation></semantics></math>-token context) under the same protocol, prompt, and per-dataset frame as the panel members, across all eight datasets.
To be thorough, the quantisation we impose is a confound worth naming, since the panel’s own members are served in <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bfloat16</span>.
It does not, however, appear to drive the gap: on the four <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> sets our <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">awq</span> run of <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-72B</span>  reaches <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70.4</annotation></semantics></math> mean balanced accuracy, against the <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="69.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>69.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">69.2</annotation></semantics></math> published for the unquantised checkpoint (Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>).
The conclusion below is therefore scoped to this quantisation, without resting on it.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A8.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ Amortised cost and break-even. ‣ Appendix H Open-judge scaling and cost ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> gives the ladder and Figure <a href="#A8.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ Amortised cost and break-even. ‣ Appendix H Open-judge scaling and cost ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> plots it.
We observe that, in general, the ladder does not close.
<span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-72B</span>  trails <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Sonnet</span> on four of the eight sets, and draws level with it or passes it on three claim-verification sets (<span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.629" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.629</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.629</annotation></semantics></math> against <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Sonnet</span>’s <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.548" display="inline" ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> (<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.630" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.630</mn><annotation Those three claim-verification sets are among the four on which <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Sonnet</span> scores lowest in the suite, each already under the better of the two frames we ran for it (Table <a href="#A6.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ Provenance of the claim-support frame. ‣ Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>).
The levelling thus says more about where the frontier is weakest than about scale closing the gap.
On the remaining four, <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-72B</span>  stays well behind: <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.10" class="ltx_text Furthermore, the open ladder is not monotone in size.
<span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-32B</span>  is the better of the two on four of the eight (<span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.484" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.484</mn><annotation ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.443" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.443</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>B judge beats the whole cheap panel whereas the <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72" display="inline" </div>
<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A deployer cannot, therefore, climb this ladder by size alone.
On average, <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-32B</span>  and <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-72B</span>  are nonetheless the panel’s closest rivals, both at <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>72.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72.6</annotation></semantics></math> suite <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">bacc</span> against the panel’s <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="73.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>73.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">73.0</annotation></semantics></math>, the former at $<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.008" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.008</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.008</annotation></semantics></math> per <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> items against the panel’s $<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.039" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.039</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.039</annotation></semantics></math> (Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Cost and deployment profile. ‣ 4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).
Neither, however, indicates in advance where it will hold, whereas the panel’s regime is read from its own members (§<a href="#S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" title="The admissibility test. ‣ 3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>).
The same insensitivity to size is reported from an entirely different direction by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Singh et al. [68]</a></cite>, whose white-box hallucination detectors span only <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.3</annotation></semantics></math> points of <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">auc</span> across an eighteen-fold range of analyser size, and who report a <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>B model outperforming its <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>B sibling.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cost.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report the compute the configurations above actually consume, then price it, so that a reader who disputes the rates can substitute their own.
Benchmarked identically –batch <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\approx}500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mn>500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\approx}500</annotation></semantics></math> input tokens, a fixed <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68</annotation></semantics></math>-token decode– the ten members run at <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>23.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23.7</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40.2</annotation></semantics></math> items per second and <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-32B</span>  at 4-bit <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">awq</span> at <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14.8</annotation></semantics></math>: per <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> items, <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">gpu</span>-seconds for one member, <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="320" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>320</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">320</annotation></semantics></math> for the panel run in sequence, and <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68</annotation></semantics></math> for the <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>B judge.
At a public reference rate for the card we used (an <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">a40</span> at $<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.44" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.44</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.44</annotation></semantics></math> per <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">gpu</span>-hour) that is $<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.039" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.039</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.039</annotation></semantics></math> per <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> items for the panel against $<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.52</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.52</annotation></semantics></math> for <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Sonnet</span> at its list token rate, about a sixty-fourth.
The ratio carries, however, two caveats.
First, it times the members one after another, so it is right for throughput but pessimistic for latency, which a deployer with several cards can cut by serving the members in parallel.
Second, one card rate serves a member and a 4-bit <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>B judge alike, whereas <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen2.5-72B</span>  does not fit the same envelope, and we therefore quote no rate for it.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Rented and owned compute.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Those dollars are a <em id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">rental</em> price, right for a deployer choosing between renting a card and buying frontier <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">api</span> calls.
For one who already owns the hardware –much of the point of an open panel– the marginal cost of a judgement is electricity, and the question becomes whether the workload fits the hardware at hand.
It does, on more modest hardware than we used.
We served the members in <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bfloat16</span>, in which a <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math>B model’s weights occupy some <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">gb</span> and call for a <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">gb</span> card.
At 4 bits they fall to roughly <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">gb</span>, which leaves room for an <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8192</annotation></semantics></math>-token cache on a current-generation <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">gb</span> consumer card.
Since the panel runs sequentially, only one member need be resident at a time.
One such card therefore hosts the whole roster by loading its members in turn.
This is a memory calculation rather than a measurement.
We did not run a 4-bit panel, so that it fits on such a card says nothing about how it would score there.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Amortised cost and break-even.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Writing <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> for the workload and <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> for the one-time calibration outlay in dollars, the panel’s amortised cost per <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> items is <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.039+10^{3}C/N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.039</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.039+10^{3}C/N</annotation></semantics></math>, which undercuts the frontier’s flat $<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.52</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.52</annotation></semantics></math> above <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\approx 10^{3}C/2.48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2.48</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\approx 10^{3}C/2.48</annotation></semantics></math>: about <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> items at the $<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> budget of §<a href="#S4" title="4. Standing in for a frontier judge ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="81{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>81,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">81{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> at $<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">200</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="403{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>403,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">403{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> were a full <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>-label set bought instead.
One assumption in that evaluation deserves naming, since it is both the most uncertain quantity here and linear in the break-even.
We price a label at $<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, two minutes of an annotator’s time at $<math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math> per hour.
Where a judgement takes seconds rather than minutes, the break-even falls by up to an order of magnitude.
Where the evidence is long or the annotator must be a clinician, as on <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, it rises by as much.
Whether the gold can be reduced or replaced –by a frontier teacher, or by spending it only where the panel is uncertain– is a question of label efficiency we do not price.
A cheap panel therefore pays for a <em id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">sustained</em> evaluation workload rather than an occasional one.
The quantity to compare is the amortised total, not the inference rate alone.</p>
</div>

<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Full per-dataset tables</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix collects the per-dataset results that the body reports only through the comparator ladder of Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and the figures of §<a href="#S3" title="3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.
We first recall the eight benchmarks in Table <a href="#A9.T14" title="Table 14 ‣ Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>, with their size after construction, the denominator each enters, and the frame each is scored under;
we then move from the single members to the full ladder of methods, and close with the aggregator contrasts and the weight the stacker gives each member.</p>
</div>
<div id="A9.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As for the single members, Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> in §<a href="#S3" title="3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> already shows the distribution of their <math id="A9.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> per dataset, and one of its marks needs further discussion here.
Its square is the <em id="A9.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">oracle</em> best single, i.e. the member with the highest <math id="A9.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> on the test set itself and so the most generous single-judge comparator;
it is neither the CV-best that decides the verdicts nor the globally best-on-average member.
Those three single-judge comparators sit side by side per dataset in Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, whereas Figure <a href="#A9.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>(a), at the end of this appendix, gives every member’s own <math id="A9.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> on every dataset, from which the oracle and the best-on-average single (<span id="A9.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Gemma</span>) can be recovered.
Moving from the members to the methods, Tables <a href="#A9.T15" title="Table 15 ‣ Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> and <a href="#A9.T16" title="Table 16 ‣ Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> give the full method ladder on every dataset, on Cohen’s <math id="A9.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> and on balanced accuracy respectively.
The ladder runs from the unweighted panel, the accuracy- and log-odds-weighted variants, the average member, and the best-on-average single, through the CV-best and oracle single judges, to the stacked panel.
Both tables report central estimates only, the <math id="A9.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> cluster-bootstrap intervals being in the released artefacts.</p>
</div>

</figure>
<div id="A9.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, Figure <a href="#A9.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ Appendix I Full per-dataset tables ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> names every member, reporting its own agreement with gold per dataset beside the weight the stacker gives it.
Read together, the two panels give the deployment-side view of §<a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3. The competence/correlation account ‣ 3. Core results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>.
<span id="A9.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Gemma</span> is the strongest member on average and draws the largest weight on five of the eight sets.
Yet the leader on the grounded tasks that decide the panel’s win still moves (<span id="A9.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Granite</span> on <span id="A9.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, <span id="A9.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen</span> on <span id="A9.p4.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>), so a deployer cannot pre-select the best judge for a new grounded domain without labels.
That selection is what the panel is meant to buy, and what fails to transfer (Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Transfer to an unseen dataset ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>).
The two orderings also differ well beyond the margin.
On <span id="A9.p4.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> the weakest member of the ten by agreement (<span id="A9.p4.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Yi</span>, <math id="A9.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=0.445" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.445</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=0.445</annotation></semantics></math>) still draws the fourth-largest weight (<math id="A9.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=+0.91" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.91</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=+0.91</annotation></semantics></math>, the second-tightest across folds of any member there).
<span id="A9.p4.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Command-R</span>, conversely, takes a reliably negative one (<math id="A9.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.52</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.52</annotation></semantics></math>, over four fold-standard-deviations from zero).
A vote weighted by each member’s own accuracy could express neither (§<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" title="Aggregation and the comparator ladder. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).</p>
</div>

<span id="A9.F10.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> Each member’s own Cohen’s <math id="A9.F10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> against gold.

<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>Dataset construction</h2>

<div id="A10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each of the eight benchmarks is reduced to a set of balanced binary items, and the reduction is not the same operation in each case.
This appendix reports the procedure per dataset for reproducibility; Table <a href="#A10.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ Choice of one pair per record. ‣ Appendix J Dataset construction ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> collects the sources, the upstream pools, and what came out of each, and Tables <a href="#A10.T19" title="Table 19 ‣ Choice of one pair per record. ‣ Appendix J Dataset construction ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a> and <a href="#A10.T20" title="Table 20 ‣ Choice of one pair per record. ‣ Appendix J Dataset construction ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> show one item from each.
Instance identifiers are positional over the resulting order, so the released content-addressed index, rather than any upstream snapshot, is what anchors a verdict to the item it was measured on (see Code and data availability).</p>
</div>
<section id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The unit of judgement.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">One item is one prompt and one verdict.
Every candidate –an answer on the question-answering sets, a claim on the claim-verification ones– is judged on its own, in its own call, against the whole of its evidence; no judge ever sees two candidates together, and two claims that happen to share a grounding document are two independent calls each carrying that document in full.
The pairing described below is therefore a property of the <em id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">item set</em> and of the statistical analysis, not of the judging task.
It fixes the class balance at exactly <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50/50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50/50</annotation></semantics></math>, which makes chance agreement <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> and the <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=2\,\textsc{bacc}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">bacc</mtext></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=2\,\textsc{bacc}-1</annotation></semantics></math> identity of Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a> exact, and it defines the unit the cluster bootstrap resamples (§<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Metrics and the decision rule. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).
It gives no judge the comparative cue that seeing a supported and a hallucinated candidate side by side would supply, which would be an easier task than the one we measure.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Pairing on the four question-answering sets.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> requires no pairing logic: its <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pqa_labeled</span>  configuration ships, for each of <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> questions, one ground-truth answer and one hallucinated answer against the same reference abstract, and we take both.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> reaches us through the <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">wandb/RAGTruth-processed</span>  mirror, whose training split we filter to <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">task_type = QA</span>  (none of the purpose-trained judges we score on these items in Appendix <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Purpose-trained cheap judges off their home benchmark ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a> was trained on this split, unlike the <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>-specific detectors cited in Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>);
grouping the resulting <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5{,}034" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5,034</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5{,}034</annotation></semantics></math> responses by their query string gives <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="839" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>839</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">839</annotation></semantics></math> questions, and from each we take the first response annotated with no hallucinated span and the first annotated with at least one, requiring the two to carry the same retrieved context and dropping the question otherwise.
Of the <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="839" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>839</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">839</annotation></semantics></math> questions, <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="681" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>681</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">681</annotation></semantics></math> supply both classes.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> is taken from the <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">generation</span>  configuration’s validation split, whose <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="817" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>817</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">817</annotation></semantics></math> questions each carry several correct and several incorrect answers.
We pair the <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">best_answer</span>  field (or, where it is absent, the first entry of <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">correct_answers</span>) with the first entry of <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">incorrect_answers</span>, and skip a question lacking either;
no question is actually skipped in practice, so exactly one pair is retained per question.
(The <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">multiple_choice</span>  configuration is not used: it poses a selection task instead of the binary judgement the suite is built on.)</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> uses the <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">InstructGPT</span>  labelled release alone (Table <a href="#A10.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ Choice of one pair per record. ‣ Appendix J Dataset construction ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>), <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="183" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>183</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">183</annotation></semantics></math> biographies of human-annotated atomic facts;
from each we take the first fact labelled supported and the first labelled not-supported, drawing only on sentences the annotation marks relevant and discarding the facts labelled irrelevant, and drop a biography supplying only one class.
Of the <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="183" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>183</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">183</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="165" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>165</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">165</annotation></semantics></math> supply both.
The benchmark in fact ships three parallel annotation releases, applying the same human atomic-fact protocol to biographies from <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">InstructGPT</span>, <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ChatGPT</span>, and <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PerplexityAI</span>;
taking one of the three holds the generator that produced the candidate text fixed within the dataset, as it is in every other set of the suite.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">In all four cases the two items of a pair share one source record, together with its evidence (where there is any), so the clustering unit of §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Metrics and the decision rule. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> contains exactly two items, one of each class.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Pool balancing on the four claim-verification sets.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> sets are built differently, as the structure of those corpora dictates.
Their reported unit is a (document, claim) row carrying a binary support label, and the claims are spread thinly over the documents: <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> supplies <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="358" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>358</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">358</annotation></semantics></math> claims over <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="355" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>355</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">355</annotation></semantics></math> distinct documents, <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span> <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{,}702" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3,702</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{,}702</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{,}135" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3,135</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{,}135</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span> <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="558" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>558</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">558</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="483" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>483</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">483</annotation></semantics></math>, and <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span> <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="558" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>558</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">558</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="384" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>384</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">384</annotation></semantics></math>.
A matched pair in the sense of the paragraph above would require one document to carry both a supported and an unsupported claim, and almost none does (one document of <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>’s <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="355" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>355</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">355</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18</annotation></semantics></math> of <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>’s, <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math> of <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>’s, and <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="53" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>53</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">53</annotation></semantics></math> of <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>’s), so pairing within the source record would reduce these four benchmarks to <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="36" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>36</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">36</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="106" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>106</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">106</annotation></semantics></math> items respectively.
We therefore balance across the pool instead.
Once the test split is filtered to the sub-dataset and the label inverted so that gold <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> means unsupported, the claims go into a supported and an unsupported pool <em id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.10" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">across</em> documents; the minority pool is taken in full and the majority shuffled under a fixed seed and cut to the same size, after which the clustering unit is recovered by grouping the selected claims on their shared document.
Which class is the minority varies: the unsupported claims on <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>, and <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>, the supported ones on <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Three consequences follow, all visible in Table <a href="#A10.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ Choice of one pair per record. ‣ Appendix J Dataset construction ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>.
First, a cluster here is a <em id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">document</em> and not a pair, so it holds however many of that document’s claims the selection happened to retain (one to four, the maximum being four on <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>) and those claims need not be of opposite classes.
Second, the retained fraction is set by the upstream class imbalance, severe on <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span> (<math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="501" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>501</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">501</annotation></semantics></math> supported claims against <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>57</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57</annotation></semantics></math>) and <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span> (<math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}971" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,971</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}971</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="731" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>731</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">731</annotation></semantics></math>), mild on <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>, negligible on <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>;
<span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>’s <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=114" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>114</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=114</annotation></semantics></math>, which is why it is held back from the primary denominator, is thus forced by the source annotation.
Third, because most documents contribute a single claim, the cluster resample of §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Metrics and the decision rule. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> is close to an item resample on these four, tightly so on <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> and <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span> and less so on <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span> and <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>, whereas it binds fully on the other four, where every cluster is a pair.
Class balance is exact on all eight sets either way, which is what the <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=2\,\textsc{bacc}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">bacc</mtext></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=2\,\textsc{bacc}-1</annotation></semantics></math> identity of Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Comparability with published results ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a> requires.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Choice of one pair per record.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Three of the question-answering sets carry more candidates than we use: pooling every eligible one and balancing the classes globally, as we do on the claim-verification sets, would give <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5{,}200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5,200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5{,}200</annotation></semantics></math> items on <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> against the <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}634" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,634</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}634</annotation></semantics></math> we score, <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{,}128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3,128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{,}128</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> against <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}362" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,362</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}362</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{,}942" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3,942</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{,}942</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> against <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="330" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>330</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">330</annotation></semantics></math>.
(<span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> is not among them: it ships exactly one candidate of each class per question, so we already use all of it.)
The reason we do not is that those candidates are concentrated in very few records –a single <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> biography supplies up to <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="47" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>47</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">47</annotation></semantics></math> annotated facts, a <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> question up to <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math> answers, a <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> query up to <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math> responses– and the clustering unit is the record.
Scoring all of them would multiply items without multiplying clusters: <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> would still rest on <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="183" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>183</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">183</annotation></semantics></math> biographies and <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> on <math id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="817" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>817</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">817</annotation></semantics></math> questions, which is what the interval width is governed by, whilst one verbose biography would come to weigh as much as twenty terse ones in every point estimate.
Taking one pair per record instead gives every record equal weight, and it is also what the claim-verification sets do in effect, those corpora supplying about one claim per document to begin with.
The choice has a cost, albeit a bounded one.
It discards annotation that would have sharpened the within-record picture, and, in exchange, each item pair comes from a distinct record.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A10.T18" class="ltx_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:70%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A10.T18.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:129%;">Table 18</span>. </span><span id="A10.T18.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:129%;">Reduction of each benchmark to balanced binary items (Appendix <a href="#A10" title="Appendix J Dataset construction ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">J</span></a>).
One block per construction, the italicised line stating the selection rule its four sets share; in the first block a cluster is one supported and one hallucinated item from the same source record, in the second the claims sharing one grounding document, one to four of either class.
Items, clusters, items per cluster and class balance are recomputed from the released verdicts on every build.</span></figcaption><div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<div id="A10.T18.8" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:108.8pt;vertical-align:-53.6pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-190.9pt,60.2pt) scale(0.474742477016378,0.474742477016378) ;">
<table id="A10.T18.8.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">

<section id="A11" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix K </span>Judge roster, prompt, and coverage</h2>

<section id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The roster.</h4>

<div id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A11.T21" title="Table 21 ‣ The roster. ‣ Appendix K Judge roster, prompt, and coverage ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a> names the ten members in full: the exact instruction-tuned checkpoint each tag stands for, the developer behind it, and the reference describing it.
No two members share a developer, which is the sense in which the families are disjoint, i.e. the panel is not ten fine-tunes of one lineage.
The index column is the roster position, which matters for the measurement rather than for the analysis: a run is sharded and cached by it, whereas every released verdict names its member by the full checkpoint name.</p>
</div>
