<section id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prompt and decoding.</h4>

<div id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Within a dataset, every judge, panel member and frontier alike, receives the same fixed prompt, so that no within-suite contrast is confounded by a difference in wording.
The four question-answering sets are scored under the condition we label <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">def_on</span>.
We reproduce its template below in its <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> instantiation, verbatim but line-wrapped to the page, with <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;…&gt;</span> marking the fields filled in per item.
The three other sets differ from it only in the two respects named after the listing.</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para"><pre id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">
You are assessing a candidate answer to a medical research question. You
are given the question, reference evidence, and one candidate answer.

Definition. A HALLUCINATED answer contains information that is incorrect,
fabricated, or not supported by the evidence: e.g. it misreads the
question, reverses a finding, invents a mechanism, or adds specifics
absent from the source. A SUPPORTED answer is fully consistent with the
truth/evidence.

Decide whether the candidate answer is a HALLUCINATION.

Think briefly (1-2 sentences), then end with exactly one line:
VERDICT: &lt;HALLUCINATED or SUPPORTED&gt;

# Question
&lt;the question&gt;

# Reference knowledge
- &lt;the reference passage(s)&gt;

# Candidate answer
&lt;the candidate answer&gt;
</pre>
</div>
<div id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Only two things vary across those four sets.
The first is the noun phrase naming the task (“a medical research question” on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, “a retrieval-augmented question” on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>, “a general-knowledge question” on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>, “a biographical claim” on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span>).
The second is the evidence block, whose heading names the source at hand (<span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Reference knowledge</span> on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Retrieved passages</span> on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span>).
On the two ungrounded sets this block drops out altogether, together with the clause announcing it, leaving the question, the candidate, and the same rubric.</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The four <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LLM-AggreFact</span> sets are scored under the claim-support frame of §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" title="Benchmarks and judges. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, which replaces the question–candidate scaffolding with a document and a claim whilst holding the reasoning budget and the verdict contract identical:</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5" class="ltx_para"><pre id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p5.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">
Determine whether the claim below is fully supported by the document. A
claim is SUPPORTED if every piece of information in it is stated in or
directly entailed by the document; it is HALLUCINATED if it adds, alters,
or implies anything the document does not support.

Think briefly (1-2 sentences), then end with exactly one line:
VERDICT: &lt;HALLUCINATED or SUPPORTED&gt;

# Document
&lt;the source document&gt;

# Claim
&lt;the claim&gt;
</pre>
</div>
<div id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Decoding is greedy (temperature <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>, a single sample) at an <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8192</annotation></semantics></math>-token context, so each judge returns one verdict per item.
That verdict is therefore deterministic up to the numerical noise of batched serving, whose size the re-run reported under Code and data availability measures.
The ten members and the two open judges were served with vLLM, for the most part on a host with two NVIDIA <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">a40</span> <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">gpu</span>s with a single NVIDIA <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">a6000</span> as a fallback, and the frontier judge was queried through the Anthropic <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">api</span>.
Every member is run at that full context, matching the frontier judge, so there is no input-truncation asymmetry between the panel and the single-judge baselines on the long-document sets.
The verdict is read from the last <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">VERDICT:</span> line the reply contains; failing that, from the last of <em id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">hallucinated</em> or <em id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.1.7" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">supported</em> to appear in its final <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">200</annotation></semantics></math> characters, which recovers a judge that answers correctly but drops the required prefix.
A reply that yields neither is recorded as an abstention rather than forced into a class.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Coverage.</h4>

<div id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A11.T22" title="Table 22 ‣ Coverage. ‣ Appendix K Judge roster, prompt, and coverage ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a> audits what that parsing rule leaves: per-member coverage, the fraction of items on which a member returned a parseable verdict, under each dataset’s own frame.
Abstentions are rare in the aggregate, running to some <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the ten-judge votes across the suite, and it is those that the stacker of §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" title="Aggregation and the comparator ladder. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> imputes to <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>.
The unweighted majority baseline treats them differently, being read over the members that committed on the item rather than over an imputed ten, and resolving a tie –possible whenever an even number commit– towards <em id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">hallucinated</em>, as the <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> threshold of §<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" title="Aggregation and the comparator ladder. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> does.
In particular, every member clears a coverage of <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.95</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.95</annotation></semantics></math> (i.e., the level below which we flag a cell) on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>, <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">CNN</span>, <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span>, and <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span>.
The nine flagged cells elsewhere are <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Granite</span> (<math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.827" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.827</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.827</annotation></semantics></math>) and <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Command-R</span> (<math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.904" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.904</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.904</annotation></semantics></math>) on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span> under the definition-bearing rubric, <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Command-R</span> again on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RAGTruth</span> (<math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.923" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.923</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.923</annotation></semantics></math>), and, on the claim-verification sets, <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Phi</span> (the lowest of the suite, at <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.523" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.523</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.523</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> and <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.756" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.756</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.756</annotation></semantics></math> on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>) together with <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Llama</span>, <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Falcon</span>, and <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GLM</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Two properties of this audit matter for the results.
First, coverage is measured on the condition each dataset is actually analysed under, not pooled across the conditions a member was ever run on, so the table reports exactly the votes that enter the numbers above.
Second, a member’s coverage only reaches a headline contrast when that member <em id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">is</em> the contrast, i.e. when it is the CV-best single judge being compared against the panel;
on every other cell the stacker simply imputes the missing vote (§<a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" title="Aggregation and the comparator ladder. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).
Five of the eight CV-best baselines do abstain somewhere, but four of them only marginally (<span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span>, <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">XSum</span>, and <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">TruthfulQA</span> commit on <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> or more of their items, <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">FActScore</span> on <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>97.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97.3\%</annotation></semantics></math>);
only <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>’s <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Granite</span>, at <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="82.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>82.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">82.7\%</annotation></semantics></math>, under-covers materially, which is why the confound examined next singles that dataset out.</p>

<section id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Abstention encoding.</h4>

<div id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Feeding an abstention to the meta-learner as <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> enters it in Equation <a href="#S2.E1" title="Equation 1 ‣ Aggregation and the comparator ladder. ‣ 2. The RAIM protocol ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> through the same linear term as a committed vote, which asserts that a missing verdict lies midway in log-odds between <em id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">supported</em> and <em id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">hallucinated</em>.
An abstention that arises from an unparseable generation, a refusal, or a context overflow, rather than from a member’s considered indifference, might however mean something different in principle.
We therefore measure what fixing this constant costs.</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A11.T23" title="Table 23 ‣ Abstention encoding. ‣ Appendix K Judge roster, prompt, and coverage ‣ RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a> refits the panel with the abstention encoded as a <em id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">category</em> instead –a one-hot over <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0,1,\mathrm{abstain}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>abstain</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0,1,\mathrm{abstain}\}</annotation></semantics></math> per member, taking the features from ten to twenty– holding the folds, the seed, the items, the estimator, the penalty, and the decision threshold fixed, so that the two arms differ in the feature map alone.
Every one of the eight paired differences is unresolved.
The largest in magnitude stands at <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.009" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.009</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.009</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, under a third of the smallest effect the paper claims, and the mean at <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.001</annotation></semantics></math>.
The bound is tightest where it is most informative: on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MedHallu</span>, the best-powered set carrying material abstention, the interval excludes any effect beyond <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.010" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.010</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.010</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, and on <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">ExpertQA</span>, the set with the most abstentions in absolute terms, beyond <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.028" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.028</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.028</annotation></semantics></math>.
Conversely, <span id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">WiCE</span> is the one set where the encoding has real room to matter and the sample no power to say so, its <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> abstention rate sitting on <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="222" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>222</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">222</annotation></semantics></math> items, so its interval is uninformative rather than reassuring.
A missing-indicator parameterisation of the same three-level factor –the committed vote, filled to <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>, beside an abstention flag– returns <em id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">identical</em> verdicts on every item of every dataset, so the <math id="A11.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> penalty’s dependence on the chosen basis contributes nothing to the comparison.
On this evidence, the results do not rest on the imputation, which we read as a convenience rather than as a modelling commitment.
A roster abstaining far more than ours would, however, deserve the question asked again.</p>
</div>

<em id="A11.T23.14.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">count</em> and <em id="A11.T23.14.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">rate</em> give the abstentions among that dataset’s ten-judge votes, and <em id="A11.T23.14.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">moved</em> the items on which the two arms return different verdicts.
The <em id="A11.T23.14.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">suite</em> row totals the eight, its rate being 1,640 of 76,700 votes; the <math id="A11.T23.m61" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A11.T23.m62" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> columns do not aggregate and are left unset there.</span></p></div></div>
